types.name: FAcesOutputTransform
types.doc:
The ACES output transform (Academy Color Encoding System 1.0: the Reference
Rendering Transform followed by an Output Device Transform), and the shaper
a baked display LUT is indexed through. Tonemap operator 4 runs the shader
twin of these functions (Shaders/Private/PostProcess/AcesOutput.hlsli), operator 5
replaces them with a .cube LUT indexed through DisplayLutShaper. This CPU
copy is the reference the shader follows step for step — the tests pin the
transform here and compare the GPU against it.

Scene-linear input is the engine's working space: Rec.709 primaries, D65.

types.name: FCapsuleShadows
types.doc:
Capsule shadows (UE's): a skinned character casts soft occlusion through a
handful of capsules that stand in for its limbs, instead of through its
triangles. The shadow map is too coarse to ground a character — the feet
float, the indirect light under a crouching body is untouched — and the
capsules are cheap enough to evaluate per pixel with a wide, soft cone.

This is the CPU half: turning a posed skeleton into capsules, and the
reference of the per-pixel occlusion Lighting/CapsuleShadows.hlsl computes
(the shader follows these functions step for step, so the tests pin the
maths without a GPU).

members.name: kMinBoneLength
members.doc:
A bone shorter than this (in skeleton units, before radiusScale) does
not get a capsule: fingers, toes and twist helpers only add cost, and a
capsule thinner than a finger casts nothing the cone can resolve.

members.name: kRadiusPerLength
members.doc:
Capsule radius as a fraction of its bone's length. A limb is about a
quarter as thick as it is long; the proxies err thin, because a capsule
wider than the limb shadows the air beside it.

between the two joints in world space. globalPose is the animator's
mesh-space pose (AnimatorComponent::globalPose); model places the mesh.
Keeps the kMaxCapsulesPerMesh longest bones. Appends to out.

types.name: FDeviceProfiles
types.doc:
A named device with known hardware gets cvar values on top of its resolved
tier, the way UE5's DeviceProfiles.ini carries a SteamDeck profile apart
from the sg.* levels. The tier alone could only say "Low" for a Deck, and
Low is the one preset with global illumination off, so the main platform of
a lighting-driven game rendered without GI — nothing sat between "Low with
no GI" and "Medium with all of it".

A profile writes a cvar only while it still holds its unclaimed value, so
config, the command line and the settings UI keep winning, and only when
the resolved tier is at or below the profile's ceiling: a platform that
recommends a higher tier for the same device keeps that tier untouched.

or null when none matched or the tier is above its ceiling.

types.name: FDirtyRangeUpload
types.doc:
Uploads only the parts of a per-frame CPU array that differ from what the
target buffer already holds. The renderer rebuilt its instance-transform and
previous-model pools every frame and wrote them whole, so a static scene
streamed the same matrices into write-combined (and on D3D12, copy-queued)
memory every frame. One instance tracks ONE buffer: it keeps a CPU copy of
that buffer's contents, so the per-frame-in-flight buffers each need their
own, and a buffer that is recreated (or a different buffer handed in) is
written whole once.

members.name: Diff
members.signature: void Diff(const void* target, const void* data, uint64_t size, uint64_t granularity, uint32_t mergeGap, uint32_t maxRanges, std::vector<FRange>& outRanges)
members.doc:
Compares `size` bytes of `data` against the tracked copy in steps of
`granularity` bytes and returns the byte ranges to write, coalescing
runs closer than `mergeGap` steps; past `maxRanges` runs it returns one
range spanning every change. The tracked copy is updated as if the
ranges were written. `target` identifies the buffer: a different one
than last time means its contents are unknown and everything is dirty.

members.name: Upload
members.signature: void Upload(StorageBuffer* buffer, const void* data, uint64_t size, uint64_t granularity, bool enabled)
members.doc:
Diff + SetData per range. `enabled` false writes everything (the A/B
fallback) and still keeps the tracked copy current.

members.name: UploadVersioned
members.signature: void UploadVersioned(StorageBuffer* buffer, const void* data, uint64_t size, uint64_t granularity, bool enabled, uint64_t version)
members.doc:
Upload, skipped outright when the caller's `version` of `data` is the
one this buffer was last brought up to (same buffer, same size): a
static scene compared its whole transform mirror byte by byte against
the tracked copy every frame only to find nothing to write. The caller
bumps the version on every change to the array.

members.name: IsEnabled
members.doc: r.GpuScene.DirtyUpload: 1 = write only changed ranges, 0 = whole buffer.

types.name: FGpuSceneSlots
types.doc:
Stable GPU-scene slots: a primitive keeps the same index into the persistent
transform buffer for as long as it keeps being submitted. The instanced
passes used to read their matrices from a pool packed per frame in draw
order — camera-visible members first — so turning the camera moved every
matrix to a new address and the dirty-range upload had nothing to skip.
With a slot per primitive the pools become lists of slot indices, the
transform buffer only changes where something actually moved, and the
instance cull compacts four-byte indices instead of 64-byte matrices.

Pure bookkeeping, no GPU state: the renderer owns the buffers.

types.name: FLTCTables
types.doc:
Linearly Transformed Cosines (Heitz/Dupuy/Hill/Neubelt 2016) for polygonal
area lights. The GGX lobe is expressed as a linear transform M of a clamped
cosine distribution, so a polygon's integral against the BRDF becomes the
closed-form integral of a clamped cosine against the transformed polygon.

The transform table is derived here instead of being shipped as a binary
blob: for every (roughness, NdotV) cell the GGX lobe is importance-sampled,
its mean direction and its two tangential second moments are measured, and
the transform is the one that maps the clamped cosine onto a lobe with the
same mean direction and the same spread. That is the initialisation the
paper's offline fit refines; it is exact at both ends of the roughness range
(a mirror and a cosine lobe) and close between them.

The stored value is the INVERSE transform, normalised so its middle row is
(0, 1, 0) — the polygon integral is scale invariant, so four numbers carry
the whole matrix:

Minv = | x  0  y |
| 0  1  0 |
| z  0  w |

in the shading frame (T1 = view tangent, T2 = bitangent, N).

types.name: FLocalVsmPagePool
types.doc:
Paged virtual shadow maps for local lights. Every shadow view (a spot, a
rect light, one face of a point light) owns a virtual depth map of
n x n pages of kPageTexels each — up to 16 x 16, a 2048-texel map — and only
the pages the camera can see receive physical memory. Physical pages are
fixed slots in the local shadow atlas, each with a guard ring of
kGuardTexels so a bilinear compare tap at a page edge never reads another
page's depth. A resident page keeps its slot across frames for as long as
its key (the view's caster-content hash, its resolution and its page
coordinates) stays the same; a moved light or a moved caster changes the
key and the page is drawn again.

The class is the CPU half only — keys, slots, LRU eviction and the geometry
that maps a page onto its slot — so it is testable without a device.

members.name: ApplyDepthMarks
members.signature: static uint32_t ApplyDepthMarks(std::vector<uint8_t>& neededMask, uint32_t pagesPerSide, const uint32_t* marks, uint32_t markPagesPerSide, uint32_t stamp)
members.doc:

coarser page is hit when any finer page under it is, a finer page when
its parent is), and every hit is grown by one page so a penumbra or a
few frames of parallax across a page edge still finds its depth. Pages
the marks rule out become 3 (reachable, no receiver); returns how many
stay 1.

(it reads pool vertices, not the per-instance pre-skin buffer), so a
skinned graph draw without this pipeline falls back to the classic
skinned graph raster path rather than lose its graph.

both, a skinned draw stays on the classic GPU-skinned raster path.

The cull-off twin of the skinned meshlet pipeline (same shader — the
skinned task stage never had a backface cone to disable, so the twin
differs only in rasterizer cull state). Without it, two-sided skinned
draws (uber and graph alike) fall back to the classic raster path.

members.name: InstancedMdiRun
members.doc:
The group is a live MultiDrawIndirect run (leader or covered member).
Meshletizing one member would leave the leader's MultiDraw drawing it a
second time, so runs stay whole on the classic instanced path.

types.name: FMeshletSwRasterTraits
types.doc:
Everything the plan knows about one already-meshlet-eligible draw that
decides whether its clusters may take the SOFTWARE rasterizer. The per-
CLUSTER decision is the task stage's (projected cluster size); this is the
per-DRAW gate above it, and it exists because admitting a draw that
contributes no software cluster is not free: a table-resident material joins
the batched resolve pass but widens its scissor to the draw's whole
projected extent, and a material that needs its own descriptor set cannot be
batched at all and buys a whole screen pass.

members.name: PipelinesReady
members.doc:
Both the raster compute pipeline and the resolve graphics pipeline. The
visibility buffer is useless without the resolve — a cluster routed to
software with no resolve to read it back is a hole in the G-Buffer, so
the pair is one gate, never two.

members.name: Skinned
members.doc:
Skinned clusters live in a per-instance pre-skin buffer addressed by a
device address in the mesh push block; the raster compute reads the
shared pool instead and would rasterize the bind pose.

members.name: GraphMaterial
members.doc:
A graph material displaces vertices in the mesh stage (WPO) and shades
through its own per-hex permutation. The software rasterizer transforms
pool vertices with no evaluator, and the resolve pass is the uber pixel
shader — a graph draw would rasterize undisplaced and shade flat.

members.name: DrawPixelDiameter
members.doc:
Projected screen diameter of the whole draw's bounding sphere. Clusters
only ever project smaller than the draw that holds them, so a draw above
the ceiling is dominated by hardware-sized clusters and would buy a
resolve pass for a handful of pixels.

members.name: kWpoUnboundedThreshold
members.doc:
Above this the graph compile's wpoBound is the unboundable-subtree
sentinel (MaterialGraph::kWpoBoundUnbounded = 3e38). Must match the
task shaders' `wpoBound > 1e30` test — the CPU-side culls mirror the
same rules.

members.name: WpoInflatedCullRadius
members.signature: static float WpoInflatedCullRadius(float boundsRadius, float wpoBound)
members.doc:
The classic-path mirror of the meshlet task stage's WPO cull rules:
graph WPO displaces vertices after the model transform, so any sphere
cull must grow by the material's conservative |WPO| bound or a draw
displaced across the frustum/cascade boundary disappears. Returns the
inflated radius; a negative return means the draw must not be sphere-
culled at all (the unbounded sentinel — guessing a radius could cull
live geometry). A non-positive boundsRadius passes through unchanged:
it already marks the draw uncullable by convention (skinned casters).

members.name: ProjectedPixelDiameter
members.signature: static float ProjectedPixelDiameter(float radius, float distance, float projScale)
members.doc:
Screen diameter, in pixels, of a world-space sphere of `radius` whose
centre sits `distance` from the camera. `projScale` is the meshlet
path's own LodParams.y (0.5 * renderHeight * Proj[1][1]) — pixels per
world unit at unit distance — so the cut, the page budget and this
share one projection constant and cannot disagree about scale.

The denominator is clamped to just outside the sphere: a camera INSIDE
a cluster's bounds has no meaningful projected size, and letting the
distance go to zero would return an enormous diameter that reads as
"hardware" by accident rather than by decision. The task shader
evaluates this same expression.

members.name: IsSoftwareCluster
members.signature: static bool IsSoftwareCluster(float radius, float distance, float projScale, float thresholdPixels)
members.doc:
The split: at or below `thresholdPixels` across, a cluster's ~124
triangles are at or under a pixel each and the hardware setup/raster
cost per triangle dominates the shaded pixels, which is exactly the
regime a compute rasterizer wins. Above it, hardware raster keeps the
cluster. A non-positive projScale (LOD disabled) or a camera inside the
cluster keeps hardware — never guess a split when the projection the
rule is written in does not hold.

members.name: kSwResolvePassNone
members.doc:
Resolve-pass ids. The resolve reads its pass id per pixel out of the
material entry the record names and discards everything that belongs to
another pass, so these are the whole arbitration between passes.
0  = no pass owns the slot. Its owner draw never recorded (skipped, or
gone from the frame after the plan reserved the slot), so it
carries no shading state at all and shading its pixels would paint
a zeroed material block black.
1  = the batched pass. Every material that is fully table-resident goes
here: those bind the SHARED default descriptor set on the hardware
path too, so the set-1 bind is identical for all of them and the
only remaining per-material state — the 176-byte block — is read
per pixel from the material SSBO. That is what collapses one pass
per material into one pass.
2+ = one pass per material that still needs its OWN descriptor set (a
standalone opacity mask, a partially-resident texture set,
bindless off). Those cannot be batched: a descriptor set is bound
per draw, not indexed per pixel.

members.name: AssignSwResolvePasses
members.signature: static uint32_t AssignSwResolvePasses(const uint8_t* recorded, const uint8_t* batchable, uint32_t count, uint32_t* outPassIds)
members.doc:
Fills `outPassIds` (count entries) and returns how many passes the
resolve will record. Nonzero `recorded[i]` = the slot's owner draw filled
in its shading state; nonzero `batchable[i]` = its material is fully
table-resident.

types.name: FQualityAutoTier
types.doc:
The single heuristic every host uses to resolve the scalability tier when
`r.Quality` is Auto (-1). An explicit preset (config cvars.r.Quality,
--cvar, in-game/editor settings) always wins; auto-detection only fills
the -1 "code default" slot.

The GPU decides the ceiling and the CPU decides whether we can reach it: a
strong card behind four cores hits a game-thread wall long before it hits a
GPU one, and a tier picked from VRAM alone would sell that machine a frame
rate it cannot hold.

members.name: Resolve
members.signature: static int32_t Resolve(const char* host, bool benchmarkIfMissing = false)
members.doc:
Resolves `r.Quality` for this process: leaves an explicit (>= 0) value
untouched, otherwise detects the tier from the selected GPU and writes
it to the cvar. Call after the RHI device is selected. Returns the
resolved preset value (always >= 0 once a device exists).

A cached FSynthBenchmark result for this machine feeds the detection
first. `benchmarkIfMissing` runs the benchmark (about a second, blocking)
when there is none and stores it: the player passes true so its first
launch measures the machine; the editor passes false and measures only
from the Quality menu.

members.doc:
Same contract as Resolve, for `r.Upscaler` / `r.UpscalerQuality`: an
explicit setting wins, otherwise the vendor's own temporal upscaler is
chosen when it is really available and TSR carries everything else.
Call after Resolve, with the device's live capabilities.

`authoringView` is the editor viewport. It resolves to native resolution
with a temporal AA resolve — UE5's editor default of 100% screen
percentage — because an upsampled viewport shows the artist reconstructed
pixels and shimmer that the frame they are authoring does not have. The
game keeps the tier's upscaling.

members.name: ResolveDeviceBudgets
members.signature: static void ResolveDeviceBudgets(const char* host, bool interactive)
members.doc:
Fills the remaining auto slots that depend on the live device rather
than on the tier: dynamic resolution and the streaming budget.

`interactive` is true for a shipped game and false for the editor. The
editor viewport composites through Arc into a shared swapchain, so a
viewport that resized itself every frame would fight the UI around it;
it keeps a static scale and a looser memory budget instead.

members.name: AssetBudgetForVramMB

members.name: SupportsMeshShaders

16 GB card nobody had listed could never reach virtual shadow maps,
MegaLights, ray-traced reflections or the meshlet path. Both default
false, which is the conservative answer for an unprobed device.

SceneRenderer's frame order, the SceneViewExtension idea: a plugin or game

AfterGBuffer       the opaque GBuffer (and GPU foliage) is written; nothing lit

members.name: DdgiReactScale
members.doc:
How sharply a DDGI probe texel shortens its temporal blend when the
radiance arriving at it changes for real. A fixed hysteresis is a fixed
time constant, so without this a light switching on takes the same ~73
frames a 1% drift does. Sparser probe tiers trace fewer rays, so their
change tracker is noisier and reacts less eagerly. 0 = fixed hysteresis.

members.doc:

wall at 64 texels is ~12 cm a texel, which smears the bounce off any
detail; the higher tiers buy finer cards with a bigger atlas.

members.name: AoDivisor
members.doc:
Resolution divisor for the AO trace (GTAO horizon integral / RTAO rays)
and the horizontal AO blur. The vertical blur still runs at full res with
the divided tap spacing, so it doubles as the joint bilateral upsample.
1 = full res. r.AO.Divisor overrides.

members.name: BentNormalDivisor
members.doc:
Resolution divisor for the bent-normal filter chain, floored at
AoDivisor (the filter never upsamples its own source). The GI composite
reads the result through a 4-tap depth-bilateral upsample whenever this
lands below full res. r.GI.BentNormal.Divisor overrides.

members.name: DofBokeh
members.doc:
Depth-of-field kernel: 0 = separable gaussian, 1 = circular disk gather
with fill. The disk is what produces real out-of-focus highlights and it
is strictly the better image at a bounded extra cost, so the top tiers
take it. r.DoF.Bokeh -1 follows this.

members.name: MeshLodBias
members.doc:
LOD bias in levels: the pick sees coverage scaled by the boundary ratio
this many times, so every boundary moves that many levels closer while a
close object keeps LOD0. Lower tiers push this up to shed triangles
earlier; Epic/Cinematic leave it at 0. Overridable via r.MeshLODBias.

members.name: MinScreenCoverage
members.doc:
Small-object cull: a static mesh whose world sphere covers less than this
fraction of the vertical FOV is dropped from every pass. 0 = off.
r.MinScreenCoverage overrides.

members.name: OcclusionCull
members.doc:
Hi-Z occlusion cull against last frame's depth pyramid (main view only).
r.OcclusionCull overrides.

members.name: EnableGI
members.doc:
The feature toggles the preset used to compute as `preset >= Medium`
expressions. They are data here for one reason: an expression against the
BASE preset cannot be moved by a scalability group, so `sg.*` could tune
every number a feature uses and never turn the feature off. On the
engine's own scene global illumination is 5.6 of a 10.9 ms frame, which
is a defensible design position and has to be a choice the project makes
— `sg.GlobalIlluminationQuality=0` is that choice, and it now costs
nothing else. Each stays individually refinable by its own `r.*` cvar.

gives every local light either an atlas tile or no shadow; on, the
shadow-casters past the atlas budget shade through the stochastic path.

parity with the atlas on Vulkan and D3D12 with one shadow draw fewer.

members.name: MegaLightsCheap
members.doc:
Cheap screen-space fallback shadow for shadow-casting local lights denied
an atlas tile while MegaLights is off (Low/Medium/High): a short contact-style
depth march toward the light instead of no shadow at all.

members.name: ShadowSdfFar
members.doc:
SDF far sun shadows: cone-trace the GI global SDF past the CSM range
(needs the SDF, so Medium+); step count is the quality knob.

members.name: RtShadows
members.doc:
Ray-traced sun shadows. The sample count below was tuned per tier
(2/3/4 across High/Epic/Cinematic) while nothing ever switched the
feature on, so the finished RT sun-shadow path was reachable only by
typing the cvar — the same shape the VSM tier default was missing.
Options.RTShadows carries it, and r.RTShadows -1 follows this row.

members.name: RtShadowSamples
members.doc: RT sun shadow cone samples per pixel (r.RTShadows).

members.name: MeshletGBuffer
members.doc:
Mesh-shading GBuffer path (cluster DAG + per-meshlet cull). Epic+;
no-ops back to the raster path on devices without VK_EXT_mesh_shader.

members.name: DepthPrepass
members.doc:
Depth prepass before the G-buffer (High+). A second vertex pass in
exchange for shading each visible pixel once: the trade only pays where
the G-buffer pixel shader is the expensive half, which is not the case
on the vertex-bound machines Low and Medium target. r.DepthPrepass
overrides.

members.name: VolumetricFog
members.doc: Froxel volumetric fog: enable flag + grid dims per tier.

members.name: CloudMode
members.doc:
Which cloud implementation a tier picks once clouds are switched on:
1 = the 2.5D fbm sky plane, 2 = the raymarched volume (Epic+). The tier
does NOT enable clouds — Options::VolumetricClouds / r.VolumetricClouds
still decide whether the sky has any.

members.name: CloudShadows
members.doc:
Sun-space cloud transmittance map over the deferred sun + froxel fog
in-scatter (raymarched clouds only). High+; r.Clouds.Shadows overrides.

types.name: FScalabilityGroups
types.doc:
Independent quality axes, the `sg.*` model. One tier for everything is too
blunt: a machine can be short of fill rate and long on memory, or the other
way round, and a single dial makes it give up both. Each group picks which
tier ROW its own fields come from, so the rows stay the single source of
numbers and only the selection is per-group.

Every group defaults to -1, meaning "follow r.Quality". A player or a config
that sets one explicitly pins that axis and leaves the rest automatic.

members.name: CVarName
members.doc: The cvar name a group reads, e.g. "sg.ShadowQuality".

members.name: Resolve
members.signature: static EQualityPreset Resolve(EGroup group, EQualityPreset base)
members.doc: The group's own tier when its cvar is >= 0, otherwise `base`.

members.name: EnsureCVars
members.doc: Registers sg.* once. Idempotent; called from the first tier composition.

members.name: ApplyPinnedIniSections
members.doc:
Applies the [<Group>@<Level>] section of every group pinned to a level
(a group left at -1 follows r.Quality, whose tier rows are code) and
returns how many cvars it set. Installed into ProjectManager, which
reads Scalability.ini but sits below the renderer that owns the groups.

members.name: GetComposed
members.doc:
The row the renderer actually applies: each group's fields taken from
that group's resolved tier. With every sg.* left at -1 this is exactly
Get(base), so the default behaviour is unchanged.

members.name: ApplyProjectRenderFeatures
members.doc:
Zeroes every enable in `row` whose project switch is off
(FProjectRenderFeatures). GetComposed ends with it; Get() stays the raw
row so the table itself can be read and tested.

types.name: FSceneParticleCollisionField
types.doc:
The scene as particles can hit it, assembled from what the renderer already
keeps on the CPU: GI's baked distance-field composite for the primary
tier and last frame's coarse depth pyramid for the fallback.

Both exist because they answer different questions. The distance field is a
world-space volume, so it covers geometry behind the camera and behind other
geometry with a real signed distance and gradient. The depth pyramid only
knows the front-most rasterized surface at 256x256, max-reduced — available
on tiers that build no distance field, wrong the moment a particle leaves
the view.

Rebound to the frame's matrices once per view; sampling is const and does no
GPU work, which is what makes it safe to call once per particle.

members.name: Refresh
members.doc:
Refreshed per view before the simulation reads the field. wantSdf is
whether any CPU emitter can collide against the distance field: asking
for the snapshot makes the renderer copy the whole field back, which on
D3D12 drained the GPU queue once a frame in every scene with a particle
system, colliding emitters or not.

members.signature: All = Shadow | Geometry | Lighting | Skybox | Transparent | DebugDraw | PostProcess

types.name: ViewMode
types.doc:
Viewport view modes (UE5-style). Values 1..12 are branches in the deferred
lighting shader (DeferredLighting.hlsl consumes the numeric value through the
lighting UBO — keep them stable). Velocity/GlobalIllumination/Reflections are
"final blit" modes: the frame renders fully lit, then a terminal fullscreen
pass replaces the presented image with the visualized intermediate target.

members.name: Wireframe
members.doc: depth/normal edge detection (true raster wireframe = future pass)

members.name: Unlit
members.doc: base color + emissive (the scene with lighting removed)

members.name: Normals
members.doc: world-space normal as RGB

members.name: Depth
members.doc: linearized depth, grayscale

members.name: Roughness
members.doc: GBuffer roughness channel

members.name: Metallic
members.doc: GBuffer metallic channel

members.name: BaseColor
members.doc: raw GBuffer albedo (no emissive)

members.name: Emissive
members.doc: GBuffer emissive channel

members.name: AmbientOcclusion
members.doc: material AO x GTAO

members.name: ShadowCascades
members.doc: CSM cascade selection tinted over grayscale sun lighting

members.name: DetailLighting
members.doc: full BRDF over neutral-gray albedo (normal/roughness detail)

members.name: LightingOnly
members.doc: lighting over white albedo, emissive removed

members.name: Velocity
members.doc: per-object motion vectors (final blit of the velocity target)

members.name: GlobalIllumination
members.doc: GI resolved indirect radiance (final blit)

members.name: Reflections
members.doc: SSR temporal reflection target (final blit)

members.name: PathTracing
members.doc: progressive Monte-Carlo reference render (ray query), tonemapped

members.name: CustomDepth
members.doc: the custom depth target, linearised (final blit)

members.name: CustomStencil
members.doc: the custom stencil target, one colour per value (final blit)

members.name: LightComplexity
members.doc: local lights reaching the pixel's cluster, as a heat map (lighting shader)

members.name: Overdraw
members.doc: opaque fragments rasterised per pixel, as a heat map (debug pass + final blit)

members.name: LodColoration
members.doc: the LOD level each mesh drew at, one colour per level (debug pass + final blit)

types.name: EQualityPreset
types.doc:
Scalability tiers (UE5-style). A preset flips the render-feature Options
flags to a sensible bundle so a shipped game gets the flagship stack ON at
a chosen tier by default instead of the bare baseline. Applied via
SceneRenderer::ApplyQualityPreset / SetQualityPreset and the `r.Quality`
cvar; CLI test scenes still set individual flags explicitly.

members.name: Low
members.doc: bare baseline — flagship features off, culling/LOD on

members.name: Medium
members.doc: clustered lighting + auto-exposure + screen-space SSS + SDF/DDGI GI (Low is the only tier without GI)

members.name: High
members.doc: Medium with the larger GI/shadow budgets (default)

members.name: Epic
members.doc: High + SSGI + SDF reflections + VSM + signed SDF

types.name: FSkyLightState
types.doc:
A SkyLightComponent flattened for the renderer. Scene::OnRender walks
the world and hands the active one over; the renderer resolves it into the
visible sky (cubemap or procedural atmosphere) AND the sky radiance the GI
probe-miss / no-IBL ambient use, so both always come from the same source.

members.name: SkyRotation
members.doc:
Yaw of the environment about world up, RADIANS (the component authors
degrees). Rides the sky-light state rather than a renderer field so it
arrives through the same produce/consume double buffer the rest of the
sky does — a rotation applied a frame apart from the cubemap it belongs
to would swing the whole ambient for one frame.

members.name: ShadowDrawCalls
members.doc:
Caster draws into a shadow map — cascades, the local atlas, the virtual
shadow map. Counted separately because the shadow passes are the ones a
frame can pay for and never sample: a sunless scene rasterized every
caster through four identity cascades, and Cinematic ran the whole
virtual chain under a lighting permutation that cannot read it. Neither
moved the main draw count at all.

members.name: VsmShadowDrawCalls
members.doc:
The virtual shadow map's share of ShadowDrawCalls, so a row can tell
"the cascades dropped their mesh casters" from "the VSM stopped".

members.name: VelocityDrawCalls
members.doc:
Motion-vector draws. Counted separately for the same reason the shadow
ones are: the velocity pass re-rasterizes the opaque list a second time
and, unlike the GBuffer, records one draw per command with no instance
grouping — a cost that was invisible here because nothing counted it.

types.name: FFogVolumeDesc
types.doc:
A FogVolumeComponent flattened for the froxel fog pass. Scene::OnRender walks
the world and submits one per enabled volume; the fog inject compute reads
them from an SSBO and adds their density/albedo/emissive to the height fog
wherever a froxel lands inside. Box uses InvModel (world -> local unit cube,
interior |local| <= 1); sphere uses SphereCenter/SphereRadius.

members.name: OffsetTex
members.doc:
Retopologize XZ offsets (RG16F, terrain-local meters), null while the
render grid is still regular.

types.name: FWorldWidgetQuad
types.doc:
A world-space UI widget flattened for the quad pass. The host renders the
widget's Arc tree into Texture (offscreen), builds Model (a camera-facing
billboard or a transform-oriented plane, already in world space, unit quad
centered on the origin), and submits one per visible world widget. The quad
pass projects Model by the view-projection, samples Texture and manually
depth-tests against the GBuffer so scene geometry occludes it. EntityId lets
interaction map a hit back to the owning entity.

types.name: FPostGraphSlices
types.doc:
Pass-slice bounds [begin, end) into the unified frame render graph.
RECORDED by BuildPostProcessGraph as it registers each slice (PassCount()
snapshots) instead of hand-numbered constants, so inserting a pass no
longer renumbers every later slice and trips the pass-count assert.
Compile preserves registration order (it is already topological); each
slice runs at its own frame point, and a disabled slice skips without
shifting later indices.

members.name: GtaoBegin
members.doc:
AO slice = compute + blur H/V + RTAO temporal tail (the tail runs only
under RT AO — the GTAO path stops at GtaoEnd - 1).

members.name: RtSunBegin
members.doc:
RT sun shadows: TLAS cone trace + temporal accumulation, feeding the
resolve the lighting pass samples.

members.name: MegaCompositeBegin
members.doc:
MegaLights composite: the denoised stochastic radiance blended onto the
freshly-lit HDR, before the sky.

members.name: SsgiBegin
members.doc:
Screen-space GI: gather into a transient, temporal into the history
pair, additive composite onto the HDR — after the DDGI composite, which
runs outside the graph between the two slices.

members.name: LocalExposureBegin
members.doc:
Local exposure's base layer: the 1/8 log-luminance downsample and its
separable blur, read by the tonemapper. Empty under r.RDG.PostChain 0.

members.name: SssBegin
members.doc:
Screen-space subsurface: blur H into an aliased transient, blur V back
onto the HDR, once all diffuse light (direct + GI) is in it.

members.name: CloudBegin
members.doc:
Clouds = raymarch into the history ping-pong + composite onto the HDR,
straight after the skybox (the 2.5D layer mode skips the march pass).

members.name: AtmosphereBegin
members.doc:
Aerial perspective + exponential height fog over the lit scene and the
sky, after the clouds.

members.name: FogBegin
members.doc:
Froxel fog = inject -> integrate along Z -> composite, between the
reflection resolve and translucency (reflections sample the un-fogged
opaque scene, glass composites over fogged opaque).

members.name: TransparentBegin
members.doc:
ReactiveCopyEnd = entry past the reactive-mask pre-copy;
TransparentCopyEnd = entry past the water scene-color copy. Both copy
passes gate inside their bodies now, so the slice runs whole from
TransparentBegin — the finer bounds remain for diagnostics.

members.name: ParticlesBegin
members.doc:
CPU billboards, ribbons and GPU emitters onto the HDR, after the
translucents and depth-faded against the GBuffer.

members.name: UpscaleBegin
members.doc:
Temporal upscaler hand-off at the head of post: the reactive mask, then
the FSR/DLSS/XeSS/TSR resolve into the output-resolution HDR. Empty when
the graph was built with r.RDG.PostChain 0.

members.name: PostMaterialBegin
members.doc: Post-process material over the tonemapped image, before TAA.

members.name: TaaBegin
members.doc:
Temporal resolve of the LDR output into the history ping-pong; the
source and both history buffers are rebound at the slice every frame.
Under r.RDG.PostChain the slice opens with the TAA reactive mask.

members.name: FinalBegin
members.doc:
FXAA / passthrough blit of the LDR chain's output into the presented
target. Registered ahead of BufferViz, which overwrites it later.

members.name: BufferVizBegin
members.doc:
Debug final-blit (Velocity / GI / Reflections view modes) — the last
colour op, replacing the presented image.

members.name: SelectionMaskBegin
members.doc:
The selected/hovered meshes into the RG8 mask the outline samples; runs
before DoF, registered here beside its reader.

members.name: PointCloudBegin
members.doc:
Scan points: splats into their own layer, the flash limiter's measure
and limit (the limit is the frame's async-compute pass), the composite
onto the presentable image. Runs after Final, before the overlays.

members.name: OverlayBegin
members.doc:
Editor/debug overlays on the presentable image after Final: the debug
lines + grid at OverlayBegin, the selection outline at OverlayBegin + 1.
Registered ahead of lens flare only so its composite stays the graph's
last transient write; they run last in the frame.

members.name: LensFlareBegin
members.doc:
Lens flare: ghosts into a quarter-res transient, then the LDR output
composited with them into a full-res transient. Never runs in a frame
that runs BufferViz.

types.name: FSubmitOrdinals
types.doc:
Per-frame submission ordinal per entity — feeds DrawCommand::submeshKey,
which keys the world-bounds cache. Version-stamped rather than cleared:
clearing the map destroyed every node, so a frame paid a malloc and a free
per submitted mesh per view just to rebuild the buckets it already had. The
stamp retires last frame's value where it lies, the same way the bounds
cache next door already does.

members.name: Prune
members.doc:
Entity ids are random 64-bit UUIDs and never come back, so without this
every mesh entity ever submitted — each projectile, spawned actor and
streamed sector entity — kept a node for the renderer's lifetime.

members.name: HasFlag
members.signature: static bool HasFlag(RenderPassFlags flags, RenderPassFlags flag)

members.name: GetLastGiAsyncJoin
members.doc:
Where the async GI update's lane joined the graphics queue on the last
primary frame: the first ALU-heavy stage or consumer ("GTAO",
"RTSunShadow", "MegaLights", "Lighting"), or "" when it ran inline.

members.name: ReflectionContinuationCutoff
members.signature: static float ReflectionContinuationCutoff(bool rtActive, float rtCutoff, float screenCutoff, bool sdfWorldReady)
members.doc:
Roughness above which the reflection ray continuation stops tracing.
Turning RT on never lowers it below what the screen and SDF legs reached.

members.name: GetCulledMeshCount
members.doc: Static meshes skipped this frame by coverage OR frustum (debug).

members.name: GetLODDrawCount
members.doc:
Static meshes submitted at each LOD this frame (lod clamped to 2).
Makes LOD switching observable in the editor profiler.

members.name: GetShadowCulledCount
members.doc:
Shadow draws skipped by per-cascade caster culling this frame
(summed across all 4 cascades).

members.name: GetCsmMeshCastersSkipped
members.doc:
Whether this frame's cascades carried only what the virtual shadow map
cannot draw (terrain, GPU foliage) because the VSM was steady and every
sun-shadow reader samples its pages.

members.name: GetOccludedCount
members.doc: Static meshes skipped this frame by Hi-Z occlusion.

members.name: GetGpuOccludedCount
members.doc:
Static draws culled by GPU-side Hi-Z occlusion in the cull compute,
read back frame-latent. Meaningful only under UseGpuDrivenCull+EnableOcclusion.

members.name: GetInstanceOccludedCount
members.doc:
Instanced-group members Hi-Z-occluded last frame, frame-latent like
GetGpuOccludedCount.

members.name: GetGpuPhase2DrawnCount
members.doc:
Two-phase cull recovery stats, frame-latent: candidates / instances
drawn by phase 2 (rejected against last frame's Hi-Z, visible against
this frame's). Nonzero on disocclusion frames, ~0 at steady state.

members.name: GetFoliageInstancesDrawn
members.doc:
GPU foliage cull stats, read back frame-latent:
instances that survived / were culled by the FoliageCullHiZ compute
(frustum + distance band + Hi-Z occlusion) across all batches, and the
number of foliage indirect draws issued this frame.

members.name: GetFoliageShadowInstancesDrawn
members.doc:
Foliage shadow-view cull stats (summed over every CSM cascade and
local atlas tile that dispatched this frame), frame-latent like the
main-view stats; plus the shadow views dispatched this frame.

members.name: EffectiveFoliageShadowCascades
members.doc:
The cascade count GPU foliage actually casts into: the
r.Foliage.ShadowCascades override when >= 0, else the tier value passed
in, clamped to 4. Static so the scalability self-test can probe it.

members.name: GetMdiBatchCount
members.doc:
Live MDI batches issued this frame (instanced-group runs merged into
one MultiDrawIndexedIndirect each).

members.name: GetMdiCountDrawCount
members.doc: How many of those batches drew through the GPU-compacted count buffer.

members.name: GetShadowRunDrawCount
members.doc:
CSM caster runs (r.GpuScene.ShadowRuns): count-sized indirect draws the
cascades issued last frame, and the instanced groups they covered.

members.name: GetLastPoolUploadBytes
members.doc:
Bytes the instance-transform and previous-model pools wrote in the last
completed frame, against what a whole-buffer write would have cost
(r.GpuScene.DirtyUpload). A static scene writes ~0 at steady state.

members.name: GetGBufferMaterialRecordCount
members.doc:
G-Buffer material records minted this frame (distinct material
flavours, record 0 included) and how many draws reused one through the
plan's per-material cache instead of rebuilding it.

members.name: GetInstancingPlanCacheHits
members.doc:
The cross-frame plan cache (r.GpuScene.PlanCache): draws this frame
whose material/mesh decisions came from an entry built in an earlier
frame, draws that had to rebuild one, live entries, and the
configuration generation every entry is checked against (it moves when
a plan-wide input — a meshlet or bindless switch, a pipeline — changes).

members.name: GetMeshDrawCommandsBuilt
members.doc:
The last scene's static draw commands (r.MeshDrawCommands.Cache): built
fresh, copied from the primitive's persistent command, and the subset
of reused ones whose material snapshot had to be retaken.

members.name: GetSubmitOrderHits
members.doc:
Of the last scene's entity submits, those that found their ordinal and
persistent entry from the previous scene's order, without a lookup.

members.name: GetShadowGraphPlanCacheHits
members.doc: The shadow plan's graph caster pipelines, cached the same way.

members.name: GetGpuSceneLiveSlots
members.doc:
Live stable GPU-scene slots, and the slots retired at the last frame
boundary.

members.name: GetGpuSceneClassicSlotDraws
members.doc:
Non-instanced draws the last plan gave a GPU-scene slot, so the
classic G-Buffer and shadow passes read their matrix by slot
(r.GpuScene.ClassicSlots).

members.name: GetVelocityPrevBySlotGroups
members.doc:
Instanced groups whose last velocity pass read the previous matrices
from the GPU scene's previous-frame mirror by slot
(r.GpuScene.PrevBySlot), 0 when the member-ordered pool served them.

members.name: GetMeshletTestedCount
members.doc:
Meshlet task-cull stats (r.MeshletGBuffer), read back
frame-latent like the other GPU counters: meshlets submitted to the
task stage, drawn in phase 0, killed per test (frustum / backface
cone / Hi-Z occlusion against last frame's pyramid), and recovered
by the phase-2 re-test against this frame's pyramid. Every counter —
including the CPU-side tested/draw-call totals — is summed over ALL
views rendered in that frame and carries the same frame latency, so
the ratios stay comparable when a frame renders more than one camera.

members.name: GetMeshletViewCount
members.doc: Scene renders that fed those counters (one per camera the frame drew).

members.name: GetInstanceGroupCount
members.doc:
Auto-instancing groups the last plan formed, and how many of them hold
mirrored (negative-determinant) members.

members.name: SetDebugName
members.doc:
Identity for telemetry. A host runs several SceneRenderers at once
(editor viewport, content-browser thumbnails, asset preview) and each
publishes its own per-instance counters, so an unlabelled log line
from one is indistinguishable from another's — two renderers each
drawing one view read as one renderer drawing two.

members.name: GetMeshletLodCulledCount
members.doc:
Cluster-DAG cut telemetry (r.MeshletLodError): meshlets killed
by the LOD cut, triangles actually dispatched (both phases), and
drawn meshlets per DAG level (level 7 bucket also holds 8+).

members.name: GetMeshletShadowTestedCount
members.doc:
The same shape for the meshlet CSM caster plan (r.Meshlet.Shadows), read
back frame-latent and kept PER CASCADE: the cut's whole return is that a
far cascade's ortho extent admits far coarser clusters than cascade 0's,
which only a per-cascade split can show. Cone/occlusion counters are
structurally absent from that pass and always read 0.

members.name: GetMeshletGBufferBatchedDraws
members.doc:
Static meshlet GBuffer draws the last plan folded into batched
dispatches, and how many dispatches carried them.

members.name: GetMeshletFallbackRuns
members.doc:
Test hooks: the batched runs the last plan sent through the meshlet
compute fallback, and the draws they cover.

members.name: GetMeshletShadowStat
members.signature: uint32_t GetMeshletShadowStat(uint32_t cascade, uint32_t slot) const

members.name: GetMeshletShadowLevelDrawnCount
members.signature: uint32_t GetMeshletShadowLevelDrawnCount(uint32_t cascade, uint32_t level) const

members.name: GetMaterialDSBindCount
members.doc:
GBuffer draws that still bind a per-material descriptor set this frame,
and how many distinct materials those cover (fully table-resident
materials bind the shared default DS instead → both drop to 0 when
every opaque material's maps are bindless).

members.name: GetVsmAllocatedPages
members.doc:
VSM physical pages mapped last frame, read back frame-latent.
Meaningful only under Options.EnableVSM.

members.name: GetVsmRenderedPages
members.doc: VSM pages re-rasterized into the atlas last frame (dirty pages only).

members.name: GetVsmCachedPages
members.doc: VSM pages served from the cache last frame (mapped − rendered).

members.name: GetVsmShadowedPixels
members.doc: Screen pixels marked shadowed by the VSM resolve last frame.

members.name: GetVsmDeferredPages
members.doc: Stale pages the per-frame budget pushed to a later frame (frame-latent).

members.name: GetVsmFullResets
members.doc:
Wholesale cache drops (first frame / VSM re-enabled after a gap). A
moving sun must NOT bump this — it goes through the stale-flood path.

members.name: GetVsmStaleFloods
members.doc:
Light-matrix moves absorbed as budgeted stale floods (mappings kept,
pages re-render over the following frames, CSM serves the stale ones).

members.name: GetVsmRunDrawCount
members.doc:
The last frame's VSM caster runs (r.VSM.CasterRuns): run draws and the
casters they covered.

members.name: GetVsmShadowImage
members.doc: Screen-space VSM resolve target (R = visibility, G = coverage) — test hook.

members.name: GetClusterLightCount
members.doc: Point/spot lights fed to the clustered cull last frame (lighting upgrade).

members.name: GetSdfVolume
members.doc: GI SDF accessors (debug/verification): the built volume + its grid.

members.name: GetSceneDepthAttachment
members.doc: GBuffer depth (full-res), the fallback tier for GPU particle collision.

members.name: SdfDimensionFor
members.signature: static uint32_t SdfDimensionFor(int32_t cvarOverride, uint32_t optionValue)
members.doc:
r.GI.SDFResolution (-1 = defer) layered over the tier/Options value and
clamped to the range the build machinery is written for.

members.name: GiSkyRadianceScale
members.doc:
The scale bound onto probe-miss sky radiance by every GI trace that
gathers sky. Public/static so a row can bind exactly what the engine
binds — a sky unit that only a shader ever sees is a unit nothing checks.

members.name: GetGiBakedIncrementalCount
members.doc:
Composites that rewrote only the voxels a changed instance could have
moved, and how many voxels the last composite (patch or full) wrote.

members.name: GetGBufferParallelPassCount
members.doc:
GBuffer passes (phase 1 and the occlusion recovery) that were recorded
through the parallel recorder rather than on one thread, and one of the
GBuffer's own attachments (0 albedo RGBA8, 1 normal RGBA16F, 2/3 RGBA8)
— together what a serial-versus-parallel parity check needs.

members.name: GetSdfDetailResampleCount
members.doc:
Detail-trace atlas work: fields resampled into a slot, and atlas uploads.
A recompose over an unchanged field set must move neither.

members.name: GetSdfSkinnedBoxUpdates
members.doc:
Skinned meshes in the GI distance field (r.GI.SkinnedSdf): the box
updates the voxelizer has run, and the skinned draws the last baked
composite placed bone fields for.

members.name: GetSdfTerrainEditBoxUpdates
members.doc:
Terrain sculpt edits taken into the GI field: near-window box
re-voxelizations, and coarse or baked windows rebuilt whole.

members.name: GetTerrainRtInstanceCount
members.doc:
CDLOD terrain tiles in the TLAS this frame, and tiles written (built or
re-displaced) / refit since the renderer started.

members.name: GetSdfOverlaySourceCount
members.doc:
Terrain and foliage in the GI field (r.GI.TerrainFoliage): the sources
and the field windows the last frame folded them into.

members.name: BuildGiLightRecords
members.signature: static uint32_t BuildGiLightRecords(const RenderFrameData& data, float emissiveScale, float emissiveRangeScale, bool emissiveEnabled, std::vector<float>& outRecords)
members.doc:
The 32-light GI list (GiLight.hlsli records), selected strongest-first
across point/spot/rect/emissive TOGETHER — truncation by submission
order dropped strong lights behind weak early ones and made the kept
set depend on scene-table iteration order (temporal instability).
Public/static so tests can pin the ranking without a renderer.

members.name: GetGiRadianceFullBakes
members.doc: Dirty-region rebake evidence: full-volume vs slab-restricted bakes.

members.name: GetGiNearRadianceBakes
members.doc:
Finer near radiance cascade (Epic): bakes so far and the extra VRAM
it costs (0 until the first bake; Epic-only).

members.name: GetGiGatherJobMs
members.doc:
Async gather (debug/verification): last gather duration on the
worker vs the render-thread consume cost, and how many gather events
ran async (FTaskGraph job) vs synchronously (first build / cvar off).

members.name: GetGiCascadeCount
members.doc:
Clipmap cascades (debug/verification): effective cascade count this
frame (1 while the scene fits cascade 0's window) and per-coarse-cascade
scroll/rebuild event counts (k >= 1).

members.name: GetGiThirdCascadeCellSize
members.doc:
The third cascade (r.GiCascades 3): its cell, and whether the chain
consumers can read it this frame (built and its radiance baked).

members.name: GetDdgiIrradiance
members.doc: DDGI probe atlas accessors (debug/verification).

members.name: CaptureDdgiBake
members.doc:
The live DDGI field as a bake, once it has converged over a scene that
fits the probe window (the grid is pinned to the scene there, not to the
camera). False with a reason in the log otherwise. Synchronous readback:
an editor command, not a per-frame call.

members.name: IsBakedGiActive
members.doc: True while a baked field stands in for live DDGI this frame.

members.name: GetDdgiProbeSlotForWorld
members.doc:
Physical atlas slot of the probe nearest worldPos (accounts for the
toroidal probe phase) — lets tests read a specific probe's irradiance.

members.name: SampleSdfCpu
members.doc:
CPU-side SDF query against the host-visible distance copy (frame-latent).
Returns the unsigned distance to the nearest surface at worldPos, or a
large value if the field isn't built / worldPos is outside the grid.

members.name: GetGiCardLitAtlas
members.doc:
GI surface cache (mesh cards) accessors, debug/verification. Nothing
outside a test reads these: the atlas is world-space renderer state with
no seam a row could reach otherwise, which is why the whole card layer
shipped measured only by inspection and CPU policy checks.

members.name: GetGiCardNormalDepthAtlas
members.doc:
The capture's own output, before the relight: a coverage census can say a
tile answered nothing but not whether the tile holds the wrong texel or
the right texel holding the wrong surface, and only this attachment
separates the two.

members.name: GetCsmStaticCacheReused
members.doc:
Last shadow pass, per cascade: restored from the static CSM cache with
the dynamic layer on top; static layer rasterized into the cache first;
drawn from scratch (its static casters moved this frame); left untouched
(its tile already held the static layer and nothing dynamic reaches it).

members.name: GetCsmStaticCacheScrolled
members.doc:
Scrolled: the camera moved the cascade by whole texels, so the cached
static layer was copied at that offset and only the uncovered strips
drew their static casters.

members.name: GetCsmStaticCacheRestoredTexels
members.doc: Texels this frame copied from the static cache into the main atlas.

members.name: GetCsmStaticCacheCovered
members.doc: Cascades a dynamic layer covered past r.Shadow.CsmStaticCache.MaxRestoreFraction, drawn whole into their own tile.

members.name: ShouldRebuildSdf
members.signature: static bool ShouldRebuildSdf(size_t evaluatedFingerprint, size_t currentFingerprint, bool evaluated)
members.doc:
The world-SDF rebuild decision, isolated so a headless row can pin it.
`evaluated` says a gather has been resolved against `evaluatedFingerprint`
— not that it produced a field. Keying the decision on "a field exists"
instead meant a window that legitimately gathers nothing (an editor camera
parked above the scene, a scene of skinned meshes only) never satisfied
its own trigger: it re-gathered, synchronously, and re-logged on every
idle frame forever.

members.name: IsSdfCpuBulkQueryable
members.doc:
True only for the baked-composite field, where SampleSdfCpu is a plain
array lookup. The legacy runtime-voxelized field answers the same query
through a per-sample GPU ReadBack, which is fine for a handful of debug
probes and ruinous for thousands of particles a frame — anything doing
bulk queries must gate on this.

members.name: SnapshotSdfCpu
members.doc:
Whole field in logical (unscrolled) cell order, from whichever build
path is live. One copy per caller per frame replaces thousands of
per-sample queries; returns false until the field exists.

members.name: BuildReactiveMask
members.signature: bool BuildReactiveMask(const Ref<Image2D>& reactivePre, const Ref<Image2D>& reactivePost, const Ref<Image2D>& mask, bool manualBarriers)

members.name: GetHiZPyramid
members.doc:
Last frame's coarse max-depth pyramid and the matrix it was rasterized
with — the depth tier of particle collision reads both.

members.name: SetParticleDepthCollisionNeeded
members.doc:
Particle collision's depth tier needs the Hi-Z downsample and its
readback even when occlusion culling is off. Demand-driven: the particle
system raises this only while an emitter carries a collision module that
can use depth, so a scene without one pays nothing.

members.name: GetNeuralGiLoss
members.doc:
The neural irradiance cache's mean training loss over the last frame it
trained (read back frame-latent; -1 before the first), the samples that
frame trained on, and the Adam steps taken since the cache was created.

members.name: GetGiBufferImage
members.doc:
The GI buffer (RGBA16F indirect diffuse, before denoise), for tests that
hold one gather against another.

members.name: GetAutoExposureValue
members.doc: Adapted auto-exposure value (read back frame-latent). 0 when off.

members.name: GetPreExposure
members.doc: Current pre-exposure scalar (1 when r.PreExposure is off).

members.name: SetMotionBlurAllowed
members.doc:
UE's editor viewports draw no motion blur outside Play: flying the
camera to place things would smear the whole view.

members.name: SetSelectionOutlineColor
members.doc:
The selection outline's colour. SceneRenderer cannot see Arc's tokens,
so the editor hands the theme's accent over every frame; the default is
the dark theme's accent for hosts that never set it.

members.doc: defined in .cpp (holds unique_ptr to fwd-declared RenderGraph)

Engine shaders are the same in every renderer, and each asset preview
stands a renderer up of its own: loading them per instance cost ~90 ms
a preview tab (Debug). One copy is shared while any renderer is alive,
with the baked IBL of an HDR (by content) and the BRDF LUT beside it.
