members.name: ApplyProjectRenderFeatures
members.doc:
Clears every Options flag a disabled project switch owns. Applied after
the tier row and again after the per-feature r.* overrides each frame,
so neither can bring back a feature the project left off.

members.name: SetRenderScale
members.doc:
Dynamic resolution (upscalers). The whole pipeline renders at
output * scale (all internal targets, incl. m_finalTarget); the upscale
to the output (presented) resolution happens for free at the consumer —
the runtime present (filtered vkCmdBlitImage) and the editor (viewport
draws GetFinalImage scaled to its panel). scale == 1 is the identity path
(render res == output res), bit-identical to the pre-upscaler renderer.
Clamped to [0.25, 1.0].

members.name: UpdateDynamicResolution
members.doc:
Dynamic resolution: nudge the render scale toward the r.DynamicRes.TargetMs
GPU frame-time target within the cvar min/max bounds. Polled at the
BeginScene safe point when r.DynamicRes is set.

members.name: GetRenderWidth
members.doc: Render (internal) vs output (presented) resolution. Equal when scale==1.

members.name: VelocityPassRanThisFrame
members.doc:
Test hooks: whether the per-object velocity pass rasterized this frame
and the sub-pixel jitter the projection carried (pixels), both for the
frame most recently recorded through EndScene.

members.name: GetFrameGraph
members.doc:
Test hook: the bound view's unified frame graph (null until the first
frame builds it) and the transient the subsurface slice blurs into.

members.name: IsLocalVsmActive
members.doc:
Test hooks: the local-light virtual shadow pages of the last recorded
local shadow pass — mapped (resident and visible), cached (kept from an
earlier frame), rendered (drawn this frame) and unmapped (wanted, no slot).

members.name: GetLocalVsmVirtualPages
members.doc: Every page of every view's virtual map, resident or not.

members.name: GetLocalVsmPartiallyKeptPages
members.doc:
Cached pages in views that also redrew a page this frame: a per-view
hash could only keep a view whole or redraw it whole, so this stays 0
unless pages carry their own caster hashes.

members.name: GetLocalVsmDepthDroppedPages
members.doc:
Camera-reachable pages left without a slot because no receiver in the
scene depth needed them, and the views whose depth marks were usable.

members.name: IsLocalVsmTwoLayer
members.doc:
Two-layer pages: whether the last pass ran with the static layer, the
pages whose static content was drawn again, and the pages that only
copied their static depth back and redrew their dynamic casters.

members.name: SetUpscaler
members.doc:
Active upscaler + quality. Selecting an upscaler/quality drives the
render scale from the upscaler's RenderScale(quality) policy: TAA/None stay
full-res (AA only); Spatial/FSR/DLSS render smaller. Requesting an
SDK-gated backend that isn't linked falls back to TAA (see CreateUpscaler).

members.name: IsDenoiseSubsumedThisFrame
members.doc:
Whether this frame's resolve owns denoising (MetalFX denoised, DLSS RR)
and how many of the engine's own denoiser bodies have run so far.

members.name: SetRespondsToUpscalerCVars
members.doc:
Opt this renderer in to the runtime upscaler console variables
(r.Upscaler / r.UpscalerQuality) — polled at BeginScene and applied at
that safe point (before the scene passes record). Only the primary view
renderers (runtime + editor viewport) opt in; secondary renderers
(thumbnails / previews) stay out so a global toggle doesn't churn them.

members.name: GetDisplayHDRMode
members.doc:
HDR display mode this renderer's output chain was built for, snapshotted
from Renderer::GetSceneHDRMode() at Initialize (0=SDR, 1=scRGB, 2=HDR10).
Non-zero switches the tonemap-and-later targets to RGBA16F and makes the
tonemapper emit display-encoded HDR. A mode change requires rebuilding
the renderer (formats are baked into targets and pipelines) — the game
runtime recreates it when the negotiated swapchain mode changes.

members.name: kPrimaryViewId
members.doc:
Multi-view rendering

A SceneRenderer owns one or more VIEWS. A view is a bundle of the
resources that belong to a camera rather than to the scene: every
resolution-sized target, every descriptor set and CPU-written uniform /
storage buffer that references them, the unified frame graph with its
transients, and the temporal history (TAA, SSR, GI, AO, previous-frame
matrices). Everything else — pipelines, shaders, samplers, the shadow
atlases, the world-space SDF / DDGI / radiance caches, reflection probe
captures, the bindless table, material descriptor caches, geometry and
meshlet pools, the particle renderers — is scene-wide and stays shared,
so adding a view costs targets, not caches.

BindView swaps a bundle in before BeginScene; every pass in between
records against that view's resources. Four views can therefore render
live into the same command buffer in one frame without overwriting each
other's uniform buffers (which would corrupt every already-recorded
pass, since the GPU reads them at execute time, not at record time).

View 0 exists from Initialize and is the primary: it alone responds to
the r.* scalability console variables and owns the shadow atlases.

members.name: CreateView
members.signature: uint32_t CreateView(uint32_t outputWidth, uint32_t outputHeight, uint32_t featureMask, float renderScale = 1.0f)
members.doc:
Create a secondary view at an output resolution, with a feature mask
(see FSceneViewFeatures) and a render scale. Returns the view id, or
kPrimaryViewId on failure. The renderer must already be initialized.

members.name: ResizeView
members.signature: void ResizeView(uint32_t viewId, uint32_t outputWidth, uint32_t outputHeight)
members.doc:
Resize a view's output. No-op when the size is unchanged; a change
rebuilds only that view's targets (WaitIdle, like the single-view path).

members.name: BindView
members.doc:
Make a view current. Must be called outside BeginScene/EndScene.
Returns false (and leaves the current view bound) for an unknown id.

members.name: EstimateViewTargetBytes
members.signature: static uint64_t EstimateViewTargetBytes(uint32_t renderWidth, uint32_t renderHeight, uint32_t outputWidth, uint32_t outputHeight, bool hdrDisplay)
members.doc:
Estimated VRAM of one view's targets at a resolution, in bytes — the
sum of every per-view attachment's bytes-per-pixel. Static and pure, so
the editor can budget a layout before allocating it and the headless
tests can pin the number.

members.name: BeginScene
members.signature: void BeginScene(const SceneRendererCamera& camera, const SceneEnvironment& env)
members.doc: New Scene API (facade over RenderFrame)

members.name: ApplyOptionsFromCVars
members.doc:
Produce-side cvar resolution (S4 write-ownership): resolves every r.*
scalability/quality knob into produce-owned m_options, then snapshots
m_consumeOptions for the render thread. Runs on the game thread before the
consume-side BeginSceneGpu realizes resources from the snapshot.

members.name: BeginSceneCpu
members.signature: void BeginSceneCpu(const SceneRendererCamera& camera, const SceneEnvironment& env)

members.name: GetProducePacketIdx
members.doc:
FScene split S6: the produce slot this frame's produce wrote (captured at
the produce/consume handoff) and the consume-side setter that points the
consume reads at it. Under overlap the enqueue captures GetProducePacketIdx()
by value and the consume calls PrepareConsume(idx) before BeginSceneGpu.

members.name: SubmitStaticMesh
members.signature: void SubmitStaticMesh(const Ref<GPUMesh>& mesh, const Mat4& transform, Material* material, EntityID entityId = INVALID_ENTITY, uint32_t surfaceType = 0, bool dynamicBody = false, uint32_t lightChannels = 1, bool castShadows = true, bool receiveShadows = true, bool customDepth = false, uint8_t customStencil = 0, bool receiveDecals = true)

members.name: SetSuppressedEntities
members.doc:
Entities whose mesh submissions this renderer drops, replaced whole: a
resident world-partition sector standing in with its HLOD proxy.

members.name: CommandCastsShadows
members.doc:
The single caster-eligibility policy every shadow subsystem (CSM
cascades, local atlas tiles + their cache hash, VSM page tracking and
raster, meshlet casters, the instanced shadow section) must consult.
Three subsystems each answering it differently is how translucent
meshes ended up casting fully opaque shadows in some paths and none in
others.

members.name: IsTranslucentShadowCaster
members.doc:
An alpha-blended draw that casts through the masked caster pipelines
with its opacity as a dither probability (r.Shadow.Translucent).

members.name: ShadowCasterAlphaCutoff
members.doc:
The AlphaCutoff lane of a caster's push block: the material's cutout
threshold, or minus the opacity of a translucent caster, which the
masked shadow shaders read as "dither by this coverage".

members.name: VsmCannotDrawCaster
members.doc:
A caster the directional VSM raster cannot draw correctly: its graph
displaces vertices (the VSM caster has no WPO variant and caches its
pages by transform) or its cutout is procedural (the VSM's MASKED
permutation clips on albedo alpha). It stays in the CSM, and its
footprint joins the resolve's uncovered mask.

members.name: WpoInflatedCullRadius
members.doc:
The single sphere-cull radius every CPU-side cull of a draw command
must use (cascade/local-tile caster culls, the GPU-driven cull
gather): the submitted bounds inflated by the material's conservative
WPO bound, mirroring the meshlet task stage's rules. Negative =
uncullable (the unbounded-WPO sentinel) — the caller must skip its
sphere test entirely, exactly like boundsRadius 0 already does.

members.name: GetSceneCameraPosition
members.doc:
Camera position of the frame being assembled (valid between BeginScene
and EndScene) — lets submitters do their own distance gating (foliage
tree meshes hand off to impostor cards past r.Foliage.ImpostorDistance).

members.name: SubmitSkinnedMesh
members.signature: void SubmitSkinnedMesh(const Ref<GPUMesh>& mesh, const Mat4& transform, const Mat4* bones, uint32_t boneCount, Material* material, EntityID entityId = INVALID_ENTITY, uint32_t lightChannels = 1, bool castShadows = true, bool dualQuaternion = false, bool receiveShadows = true, bool customDepth = false, uint8_t customStencil = 0, bool receiveDecals = true)

members.name: SubmitFoliageBatch
members.signature: void SubmitFoliageBatch(const FoliageBatchDraw& batch, const Mat4& entityTransform)
members.doc:
GPU-instanced foliage batch: one shared mesh /
impostor atlas + a persistent instance buffer, culled per-instance on
the GPU and drawn with a single DrawIndexedIndirect in the GBuffer.

members.name: SubmitDebugLines
members.signature: void SubmitDebugLines(const std::vector<DebugDrawVertex>& vertices, bool depthTest)

members.name: SubmitDebugPrimitives
members.signature: void SubmitDebugPrimitives(const std::vector<FDebugPrimitive>& primitives, EDebugDepthPriority priority)
members.doc:
DebugDraw's thick primitives (gizmo, visualisers). World draws with the
grid before the selection outline; Foreground draws after it, so the
outline of the selected mesh never paints across the gizmo on top of it.

members.name: SubmitSkyLight
members.doc:
A SkyLightComponent resolved by Scene::OnRender. The last one
submitted wins (UE5 keeps one active sky light per level). It replaces
the scene's flat ambient as the sky-lighting authority and decides
whether the visible sky is a cubemap or the procedural atmosphere.

members.name: SubmitReflectionProbe
members.doc:
A ReflectionCaptureComponent resolved by Scene::OnRender. Every capture
in the scene is submitted; the renderer captures the stale ones one per
frame and binds the highest-scoring few for shading.

members.name: SubmitPlanarReflector
members.doc:
Mirror planes for this frame. Submitted like probes; the renderer
captures at most one per frame (see ExecutePlanarReflectionPass) because
each capture is a full re-render of the scene.

members.name: SubmitFogVolume
members.doc:
A FogVolumeComponent resolved by Scene::OnRender. Cleared each BeginScene;
the froxel fog inject pass consumes them.

members.name: GetMegaLightsManagedCount
members.doc:
MegaLights engagement, for tests and the profiler overlay: how many
local shadow-casters the atlas turned away this frame (they are the
ones MegaLights shades), and whether the pass actually ran. Without
this a row cannot tell "MegaLights produced nothing" from "MegaLights
never ran", which is exactly how the feature stayed untested.

members.name: SubmitWorldWidgetQuad
members.doc:
A world-space UI widget quad resolved by the host each frame. Cleared
each BeginScene; the world-widget pass draws them where translucency
belongs (depth-tested, back-to-front). Off-screen quads are still
submitted — the pass sorts and depth-clips them.

members.name: GetLoadedSkyboxPath
members.doc:
Skybox path the renderer currently has loaded (L2 — hosts check this
instead of loading the environment's HDR a second time).

members.name: GetEffectiveSkyRadiance
members.doc:
Flat sky radiance the GI probe-miss and the no-IBL ambient use — derived
from the visible sky, never authored independently of it.

members.name: ApplyQualityPreset
members.signature: static void ApplyQualityPreset(Options& opts, EQualityPreset preset)
members.doc:
Scalability presets
Set the render-feature Options flags AND the numeric knobs (the
FScalabilityTiers row) to the given tier. Static + pure config (no
device), so headless tests can validate the mapping.

members.name: ComputeMaterialMipBias
members.signature: static float ComputeMaterialMipBias(uint32_t renderWidth, uint32_t outputWidth, bool temporalResolve, bool sdkUpscaler)
members.doc:
The texture LOD bias every material sample takes when a temporal
resolve upscales the frame — UE's MaterialTextureMipBias. A frame
rendered at 0.667 of the output grid without it picks the mip for the
render grid, and the resolve hands the display a blurred texture it can
never sharpen; log2(render / output) selects the mip the OUTPUT grid
wants and lets the jittered accumulation reconstruct it. The vendor SDKs
ask for one level more (FSR and DLSS both specify log2(ratio) - 1), TSR
and the built-in TAA take the plain ratio. Static and pure so the
headless suite pins the rule; r.MaterialMipBias.* shape it.

members.name: ComputeVsmCasterPageRect
members.signature: static bool ComputeVsmCasterPageRect(const Mat4& lightVP, const Vec3& center, float radius, uint32_t pagesDim, int32_t outRect[4])
members.doc:
VSM page-invalidation building blocks, static + pure math so headless
tests can validate them: a caster's light-space page rect (1-page
conservative margin, clamped; false = fully off-grid) and the dirty-
bitmask paint the CPU tracker uses for moved/appeared/removed casters.

members.name: PaintVsmPageRect
members.signature: static void PaintVsmPageRect(std::vector<uint32_t>& words, const int32_t rect[4], uint32_t pagesDim)

members.name: SelectVsmClipLevel
members.signature: static uint32_t SelectVsmClipLevel(float lateralX, float lateralY, float camLateralX, float camLateralY, float firstExtentSafe, uint32_t levelCount)
members.doc:
Clipmap addressing, likewise static + pure so the headless suite pins
the rules the shaders transliterate.
SelectVsmClipLevel: the finest level whose page-aligned window is
guaranteed to contain a point at Chebyshev distance d from the camera in
the light's lateral plane. firstExtentSafe is level 0's half-extent
already shrunk by one page — the window is page-aligned, not
camera-centred, so the camera can sit a page off centre.

members.name: VsmFootprintClipLevel
members.signature: static uint32_t VsmFootprintClipLevel(float footprintWorld, float firstTexelWorld, float lodBias, uint32_t levelCount)
members.doc:
VsmFootprintClipLevel: the coarsest level whose texel is still no larger
than the receiver pixel's world footprint (scaled by 2^lodBias — -1 asks
for two texels per pixel, +1 for half). Containment alone made every
receiver inside level 0's window request level-0 pages, so a far floor
at 4 cm/pixel pulled 1 cm pages it could not resolve and a wide field
exhausted the pool; the footprint is what keeps page demand proportional
to the screen, not to the world.

members.name: VsmReceiverFootprint
members.signature: static float VsmReceiverFootprint(float pixelWorldPerDepth, bool orthographic, float viewDepth)
members.doc:
VsmReceiverFootprint: world size of one screen pixel at a receiver —
view depth × the per-depth pixel size for a perspective camera, the
constant pixel size for an orthographic one. Negative depth reads as 0.

members.name: SelectVsmReceiverLevel
members.signature: static uint32_t SelectVsmReceiverLevel(float lateralX, float lateralY, float camLateralX, float camLateralY, float firstExtentSafe, uint32_t levelCount, float footprintWorld, float firstTexelWorld, float lodBias)
members.doc:
SelectVsmReceiverLevel: the level the mark and resolve passes both use —
the coarser of the containment level and the footprint level, so a page
is never requested at a level that cannot hold the point, nor finer
than the screen can show.

members.name: VsmClipLevelExtent
members.signature: static float VsmClipLevelExtent(float firstExtent, uint32_t level)
members.doc:
VsmClipLevelExtent: half-extent of a level — the first level's doubled
per level. Fixed world quantities: a camera move never changes them.

members.name: VsmClipPageOrigin
members.signature: static int32_t VsmClipPageOrigin(float camLateral, float pageWorld, uint32_t pagesDim)
members.doc:
VsmClipPageOrigin: the absolute page coordinate of a level's window
corner for a camera at `camLateral`, snapped to that level's page grid
so the window only ever moves by whole pages (a sub-page camera move
leaves every page where it was).

members.name: PaintVsmClipScrollLevel
members.signature: static void PaintVsmClipScrollLevel(std::vector<uint32_t>& words, int32_t dx, int32_t dy, int32_t originX, int32_t originY, uint32_t pagesDim, uint32_t pageBase)
members.doc:
PaintVsmClipScrollLevel: paint the pages a level's window scrolled ONTO
when its origin moved by (dx, dy) pages — exactly the wrapped-in
columns/rows, or the whole level once the move is a full window.

members.name: WrapVsmPageRect
members.signature: static void WrapVsmPageRect(const int32_t localRect[4], int32_t originX, int32_t originY, uint32_t pagesDim, int32_t outRect[4])
members.doc:
WrapVsmPageRect: a window-local page rect in TOROIDAL coordinates. A
rect wider than the grid becomes the full range; one that crosses the
wrap seam comes back with min > max, which every consumer reads as the
union of the two halves.

members.name: PaintVsmPageRectWrapped
members.signature: static void PaintVsmPageRectWrapped(std::vector<uint32_t>& words, const int32_t wrappedRect[4], uint32_t pagesDim, uint32_t pageBase)
members.doc:
PaintVsmPageRectWrapped: PaintVsmPageRect over a wrapped rect, into the
level's slice of a whole-clipmap bitmask (pageBase = level * pagesDim²).

members.name: SetQualityPreset
members.doc:
Member form: applies the row and, on a tier CHANGE, the renderer-level
one-shots (render scale / upscaler quality from the tier). Resource
recreation (shadow atlas, DDGI buffers) happens at the next BeginScene.

members.name: ApplyDefaultQualityPreset
members.doc:
Resolve the default tier (the `r.Quality` cvar when >= 0, else High) and
apply it. Called once at scene load for a normal (non-test) scene so a
shipped game boots with the stack on.

members.name: GetOutputImage
members.doc:
Output image (for editor viewport compositing). The image may be
ALLOCATED larger than the frame rendered (dynamic-res subrect in a
max-size final target) — the Valid extent is the region a consumer
may sample/blit; an SDK-upscaled frame is fully valid at output res.

members.name: GetTaaHistoryImage
members.doc:
The built-in TAA's live history (last resolve's output, sample count in
alpha as N / 32) — for tests that judge accumulation, not just motion.

members.name: GetHdrImage
members.doc:
The scene colour BEFORE the tonemap — RGBA16F, carrying radiance scaled
by the pre-exposure. A row that asserts on light rather than on pixels
has to read this: the final image is tonemapped and 8-bit, so its bright
end sits on the shoulder where any two values converge and its dark end
quantises, and a margin stated there moves with the scene's exposure
instead of with the thing under test.
Its contents are radiance * GetPreExposure().

members.name: GetVelocityImage
members.doc:
RG16F screen-space motion vectors of the last velocity pass (UV delta,
prevUV = uv - velocity). Null before the first pass.

members.name: GetCustomDepthImage
members.doc:
The custom depth pair, null until a mesh has asked for the pass
(MeshRendererComponent::renderCustomDepth). Depth is device depth in the
frame's jittered projection; the stencil target stores value / 255.

members.name: ComputeVrsRate
members.signature: static uint32_t ComputeVrsRate(float gradX, float gradY, float motionPx, float contrastThreshold, float motionThreshold)
members.doc:
Variable-rate shading (r.VRS): the per-tile rate the G-buffer pass
shades at, decided from the previous frame's perceptual luminance
steps along each axis and its motion — the CPU twin of
PostProcess/VrsRate.comp.hlsl. Rates use the shared D3D12/Vulkan
encoding: 0 = 1x1, 1 = 1x2, 4 = 2x1, 5 = 2x2.

members.name: SubmitShadowCapsules
members.signature: void SubmitShadowCapsules(const FShadowCapsule* capsules, uint32_t count)
members.doc:
Capsule-shadow proxies for this frame (FCapsuleShadows::BuildFromPose),
capped at FCapsuleShadows::kMaxCapsulesPerFrame. The pass evaluates
them into an RG8 target (R = indirect, G = sun visibility) that the
lighting and the GI composite multiply in; white when nothing cast.

members.name: SubmitVdbVolume
SubmitHairStrands
members.signature: void SubmitHairStrands(const Vec4* points, uint32_t strandCount, const FHairStrandsDraw& look)
members.doc:
One groom's render strands (FHairStrandBuilder output, pointsPerStrand
float4s a strand) drawn into the G-buffer this frame; the look fields of
`look` are taken, its FirstPoint/StrandCount are filled here. How many
strands the pass drew last frame.

members.name: GetLightFunctionTile
members.doc:
The atlas tile a light-function material path was given (-1 = none yet,
or the 16-tile atlas was full), and the atlas itself (null until the
first light with a function renders).

members.name: GetDepthPrepassDrawCount
members.doc: Draws the last depth prepass laid down (0 = the pass did not run).

members.name: GetDepthPrepassSlotDraws
members.doc:
Prepass draws that read their matrix from the GPU scene by slot (pushed
a zero model) — every one of them when r.GpuScene.ClassicSlots is on.

members.name: IsDepthPrepassEligible
members.signature: static bool IsDepthPrepassEligible(const DrawCommand& cmd, bool meshletPathActive)
members.doc:
Whether a draw may go into the depth prepass. Everything that moves a
vertex after the plain model transform, or discards a pixel, is out:
its G-buffer depth would differ from the prepass depth, and the G-buffer
pass's LessEqual would reject the surface or keep a hole where the
prepass wrote depth the G-buffer never shades.

members.name: InvalidateTemporalData
members.doc: Reset temporal data (TAA history) — call on scene switch

members.name: ClearMaterialCache
members.doc: Clear material descriptor set cache — call ONLY after Renderer::WaitIdle()

members.name: SetViewMode
members.doc: View mode

members.name: SetForcedLod
members.doc:
Pins every mesh with a LOD chain to one level (clamped to its coarsest),
static and skinned alike; -1 restores the coverage pick. Per renderer,
so an asset editor previewing LOD 2 never drags the level viewport along.

members.name: IsPathTracerForced
members.doc:
r.PathTracer.Enable is on: every view path-traces whatever its view
mode says. The viewport says so, since nothing else on screen does.

members.name: IsFogGiAmbientLive
members.doc:
The last froxel injection lit its fog from the DDGI probe field rather
than the constant ambient (r.VolumetricFog.GiAmbient).

members.name: GetPathTracerAccumulation
members.doc:
The raw accumulation (RGBA32F: rgb = summed radiance, a = sample
count), before the resolve's exposure — what a furnace check reads.

members.name: IsBufferVizMode
members.doc:
Buffer-visualization modes render single-channel/debug data through the
lighting shader — the scene chain past lighting (skybox, GI composite,
SSR, translucency, DoF/MB/bloom, styled tonemap) is bypassed so the
values reach the screen literally.

members.name: IsFinalBlitMode
members.doc:
Final-blit modes render the frame fully lit, then overwrite the presented
image with a remapped intermediate target (velocity / GI / reflections).

members.name: GetParticleRenderer
members.doc: Particle, ribbon & point cloud renderers (owned by SceneRenderer, initialized in Initialize())

members.name: ShareParticleRenderersFrom
members.doc:
Share particle/ribbon renderers from another SceneRenderer (game view uses scene view's renderers)
The shared renderers are NOT owned by this SceneRenderer (won't be deleted in Shutdown)

members.name: GizmoRenderCallback
members.doc: Gizmo rendering callback (set by editor)

members.name: SetSkyboxCubemap
members.doc: Set skybox cubemap (from TextureCube or Image2D with IsCubeMap=true)

members.name: GenerateIBLFromHDR
members.doc: Generate IBL maps from HDR file path (call after SetSkyboxCubemap)

members.name: GenerateIBLFromMemory
members.signature: void GenerateIBLFromMemory(const void* fileData, uint64_t fileSize)
members.doc: Generate IBL maps from HDR file data in memory (for VFS/MEAF)

members.name: LoadSkyboxAndIBLFromHDR
members.doc:
Load skybox + IBL in one pass: HDR → GPU equirect→cubemap → skybox + IBL
Returns the cubemap Image2D (for sharing with other renderers)

members.name: LoadSkyboxAndIBLFromMemory
members.signature: Ref<Image2D> LoadSkyboxAndIBLFromMemory(const void* fileData, uint64_t fileSize)

members.name: GetIBLCubemap
members.doc: Get the IBL cubemap (for sharing between renderers)

members.name: SetSkyboxAndIBLFrom
members.signature: void SetSkyboxAndIBLFrom(Ref<Image2D> cubemap, const SceneRenderer& other)
members.doc: Set skybox + IBL from a pre-computed cubemap (e.g. shared from another renderer)

members.name: ShareIBLFrom
members.doc: Share IBL textures from another SceneRenderer (avoids re-generation)

members.name: SetSelectedEntities
members.doc: Selection outline: set entity IDs to render outlines for

members.name: SetSkyRotation
members.doc:
Yaw the environment about world up, in RADIANS. Applies to a cubemap
sky and every lobe derived from it (skybox draw, irradiance, prefilter,
the forward path's sky miss, reflection captures) — one angle so the
sky you see and the sky you are lit by can never drift apart. A scene
with a SkyLightComponent supplies this through the sky-light state; this
setter is for hosts that submit no sky light (previews, tests).
`r.Sky.Rotation` (degrees) adds on top for quick A/Bs.

members.name: GetEffectiveSkyRotation
members.doc:
The rotation actually in force this frame, radians. Zero while the
visible sky is the procedural atmosphere.

members.name: RotateSkyDirection
members.signature: static Vec3 RotateSkyDirection(const Vec3& dir, float yawRadians)
members.doc:
CPU twin of MowoRotateSkyDir (Sky/SkyRotation.hlsli). Turning the sky by
+yaw means turning the LOOKUP by -yaw; both sides go through one
definition so the self-test can pin the direction of the rotation.

members.name: FoldSkyRotationIntoProbeHash
members.signature: static uint64_t FoldSkyRotationIntoProbeHash(uint64_t sceneHash, float yawRadians)
members.doc:
Folds the sky yaw a reflection capture is baked under into its
scene-content fingerprint (the DerivedDataCache key and the stale
test), so turning the sky retires the cubes captured under the old
one. Hashes the quantised (sin, cos) lanes rather than the angle: a
full turn keys the same bake as no turn, and slider float noise does
not re-key. Pure — pinned by the sky-grid self-test.

members.name: ComputeProbeSceneHash
members.signature: static uint64_t ComputeProbeSceneHash(const RenderFrameData& data, uint64_t skyIdentity, bool giFeedsCapture)
members.doc:
Scene-content fingerprint a reflection capture is keyed on in the
DerivedDataCache — the key a packaged game looks its baked cubes up by,
so an input missing here ships a stale capture. `skyIdentity` names the
loaded sky image (0 when none), `giFeedsCapture` says whether the
capture shades from the local light list. Pure — pinned by the
ddc-key self-test.

members.name: SetGridSpacing
members.doc: Minor cell size in world units at ground level (see Options::GridSpacing).

members.name: ResolveGridSpacing
members.signature: static float ResolveGridSpacing(float authoredSpacing, float heightAbovePlane)
members.doc:
Cell size the grid pass actually draws at. The authored spacing steps by
powers of ten with the camera's height above the plane, so a viewport
flown from 1 m to 10 km keeps a readable cell instead of collapsing into
an aliased sheet. `heightAbovePlane` is |camera.y - plane.y|. Pure —
pinned by the sky-grid self-test.

members.name: ResolveSnapGridSpacing
members.signature: static float ResolveSnapGridSpacing(bool snapEnabled, float snapIncrement, float fallback)
members.doc:
The spacing an editor viewport hands SetGridSpacing: with translate snap
on, the snap increment — the grid then shows the lattice a drag lands
on, as UE's does; with it off (or a non-positive increment), `fallback`.

members.name: ResolveGridFadeRange
members.signature: static bool ResolveGridFadeRange(float resolvedSpacing, float authoredStart, float authoredEnd, float& outStart, float& outEnd)
members.doc:
Distance fade the pass hands the shader, derived from the resolved cell
when Options leaves the range at 0: a grid is legible for a bounded
number of cells, not a bounded number of metres. Returns false when the
range is degenerate (fade start >= end), which the caller treats as
"grid off" rather than dividing by it.

members.name: GridFadeAlpha
members.signature: static float GridFadeAlpha(float distance, float fadeStart, float fadeEnd)
members.doc: Per-pixel fade the shader mirrors: 1 inside `start`, 0 past `end`.

members.name: GetGraphPsoAsyncCreatedCount
members.doc:
Graph pipelines created asynchronously, and requests answered with the
uber fallback because the material's own pipeline was still compiling.

members.name: GetGraphPsoRecordLookupCount
members.doc:
Shadow/velocity graph lookups made from inside a record region (must
stay 0), and the ones the serial plans made instead.

members.name: GetMaterialLoadPrecacheCount
members.doc:
Graph pipelines whose compile a material load started (cache misses
only — a variant already built or building is not counted).

members.name: FShutdownCallback
members.doc:
Runs at the top of every Shutdown, before the shared resources go. The
layer above the renderer installs it to drop GPU images it caches outside
any asset manager (the scene-capture fallback targets); the renderer
cannot name that layer, and a cache outliving the device is a leak report
at allocator teardown.

members.name: IsSunTransmittanceEnabled
members.doc:
r.Atmosphere.SunTransmittance: the atmosphere reddens the sun itself, so
a day/night cycle must not tint it a second time.

members.name: PrecacheAllMaterialVariants
members.doc:
Starts every graph pipeline variant a draw of `mat` can ask for — the
mesh kinds (static, skinned, instanced, meshlet), the shadow and velocity
twins its flags select, the forward pair for a translucent — and returns
how many were newly created. Each one is recorded into the PSO cache, so
a gather over a project's materials covers what play would not reach.
Not for the record path: the graph caches are unguarded maps.

members.name: PrecacheDecalMaterialVariant
members.doc:
The decal-projector pipeline of a graph material. Every graph is
compiled with a decal permutation, so nothing about the material says it
is a decal; the gather passes the materials the levels' projectors name.

members.name: MakeGraphPipelineKey
members.signature: static uint64_t MakeGraphPipelineKey(uint64_t graphHash, uint32_t variantBits)
members.doc:
The key every graph-pipeline cache above uses. Shifting rather than
OR-ing the variant in is the whole point: a hash whose low bits are
already set would otherwise make two variants of the SAME material name
one slot, and a skinned draw would pick up the static pipeline. Three
bits cover the widest variant space (variant x two-sided, blend x WBOIT);
the 61 bits left are the same content hash the material descriptor cache
already keys on.

members.name: RetryMissingMaterialGraphPipelines
members.doc:
Editor live-recompile: drops only the CACHED MISSES so a shader that
just got compiled is retried next draw. Live pipelines stay — the
RHI's ReloadShaders refreshes them in place without a destroy.

members.name: GetRtBlasCount
members.doc: RT scene stats hooks (telemetry, frame-latent).

members.name: SetLidarTraceNeeded
members.doc:
Scanner access to the live ray scene. SetLidarTraceNeeded keeps the
TLAS resident even when no other RT feature wants it; the getters hand
a shot dispatch the most recently built TLAS + its per-instance record
buffer, and the CPU-side surface/dynamic tables ResolveHits consumes.

members.name: IsVirtualTextureDiskBacked
members.doc:
Whether the virtual texture streams from a cooked tile file, and the
physical atlas's format (BC7 / BC1 from a file, RGBA8 procedural).

members.name: GetVtResidentPages
members.doc:
Virtual texturing (debug/verification, r.VirtualTexture). Resident pages
in the physical atlas, pages the last frame's feedback asked for, pages
streamed in last update, and total pages loaded since start.

members.name: HasVirtualTextureResources
members.doc:
Whether the physical atlas exists at all. The startup warm-up does not
build it unless the feature is on, so this is what says the ~21 MB is not
being held for a pass nobody asked to run.

members.name: GetSkyViewLut
members.doc:
Sky atmosphere verification: the bound view's sky-view LUT, the CPU
atmosphere the ambient integrates, and whether a sky light capture has
finished all of its time-sliced stages at least once.

members.name: ReadPointFlashGain
members.doc:
Test hook: the gain the limiter applied last frame, read back from the
GPU state (1 = the layer composited at full strength). -1 before the
first point frame.

members.name: GetDisplayLutSize
members.doc:
Whether a display-transform LUT is loaded, and its lattice size (0 =
none: operator 5 falls back to ACES RRT + ODT).

types.name: SceneRenderer::Options
types.doc: Options for controlling editor-specific rendering features

members.name: FallbackLight
members.doc: Add default directional light if scene has none

members.name: MinScreenCoverage
members.doc:
Small-object culling: skip submitting a static mesh
whose world bounding sphere covers less than this fraction of
the vertical FOV. 0 = disabled (default — zero behavior change).

members.name: FrustumCull
members.doc:
View-frustum culling: skip static meshes whose world
bounding sphere lies fully outside the camera frustum.
Default off (opt-in, like coverage cull).

members.name: EnableLOD
members.doc:
Discrete mesh LOD: pick a coarser LOD for a static mesh
as its screen coverage shrinks. Only meshes that carry a LOD
chain (ModelResource generates them on import) are affected;
others always draw LOD 0. Default off. The two thresholds are
the minimum coverage to stay at LOD0 / LOD1 (descending); below
the last, the coarsest available LOD is used.

members.name: UseBindlessAlbedo
members.doc:
Sample static-mesh material maps (albedo + normal/MRA/detail/mask/
height) from the global bindless table instead of per-material
descriptor sets. Identical output when on; draws whose every
map is table-resident bind one shared default DS — no per-material
descriptor churn. Default ON — the device mandates descriptor
indexing at creation, so any device that initialized supports it.
`r.BindlessAlbedo 0` reverts live (name kept for compat).

members.name: UseGpuDrivenCull
members.doc:
GPU-driven main-view culling. When on, the per-draw frustum
test moves off the CPU: a compute pass tests every static draw's
world sphere against the camera frustum and writes each draw's
indirect instanceCount (0 or 1); the GBuffer then issues
DrawIndexedIndirect per mesh, so the GPU decides what renders. The
CPU stops setting the frustum bit. Output-identical to FrustumCull
(same sphere/plane test). Composes with UseBindlessAlbedo for the
full GPU-driven path. CPU occlusion/small-object cull still apply
(folded in as the input bit). Default ON; `r.GpuDrivenCull 0`
reverts live.

members.name: MeshLodBias
members.doc:
LOD bias in levels, applied to the coverage the pick sees (see
FLodCrossfade::BiasCoverage). Set from the active scalability tier,
refined by r.MeshLODBias.

members.name: AutoInstancing
members.doc:
Auto-instancing: static non-skinned draws sharing the same
(mesh, material, LOD) collapse into one instanced draw with the
per-instance transforms in a storage buffer. Members are CPU
frustum-culled; groups below MinCount keep the per-draw path.

members.name: ParallelRecord
members.doc:
Parallel command recording. The GBuffer draw loop fans out
across FTaskGraph workers into secondary command buffers executed
in submission order — the GPU command stream is identical to the
serial loop, only the CPU recording cost is split. Default ON
since the visual pass (2026-07-08); `r.ParallelRecord 0`
disables live. Scenes below MinDraws keep the serial path
(fan-out overhead beats the win). Default OFF where the standard
library locks its own iterators (MSVC Debug): there the workers
queue on that lock, and the Sun Temple GBuffer recorded in 17 ms on
one thread against 28 ms in parallel. Release: 1.1 ms against 2.7.

members.name: CullShadowCasters
members.doc:
Per-cascade shadow caster culling. Skip drawing a static
mesh into a shadow cascade when its world sphere lies outside
that cascade's light-space frustum. Provably output-identical
(same clip volume the GPU rasterizer uses), so default ON.

members.name: EnableOcclusion
members.doc:
Hi-Z occlusion culling. Skip static meshes whose world
sphere is hidden behind already-drawn geometry, tested against a
depth pyramid read back from last frame. Main-view only (never
shadows). Default OFF — needs the GPU depth feed and benefits
only dense scenes; the test is a no-op until the pyramid is fed.

members.name: GpuStatsReadback
members.doc:
Read the per-frame cull/foliage/meshlet counters back to the CPU.
OFF by default because NOTHING in a shipping game reads them —
every consumer of GetFoliageInstancesDrawn and the rest lives in
The test executables — and on D3D12 a StorageBuffer::ReadBack submits a copy
and WAITS for it. A row that asserts on a counter declares this.

It does NOT make frames faster, and the measurement says so. On the
occlusion scene (Debug, D3D12, --no-throttle, 400 frames) the flag
takes the readbacks from 5 a frame to 3, but the per-call wait grows
1.39 ms to 2.18 ms and the total barely moves: 2769 ms against
2615 ms over the run, p50 unchanged at ~14.8 ms. The frame is GPU
bound, so the surviving stalls simply absorb the latency the removed
ones used to. Deleting EVERY readback does buy ~2.6 ms of p50
(11.62/12.51/12.42 against 14.07/15.27/15.02) — which is the real
finding: the win is in not BLOCKING at all (a frame-latent staging
copy scheduled into the frame's own command list), not in blocking
less often. This flag is about not synchronising a shipped game for
numbers only a test reads.

members.name: EffectsSpawnRateScale
members.doc:
Effects scalability. Particle cost in a real scene is fill, not
simulation: a smoke column is a handful of large alpha billboards
over the same pixels, and the sim that produced them does not show
up next to the blending. So the knobs that matter are the ones that
reduce covered pixels — fewer particles, smaller pools, a shorter
cull distance, a hard ceiling on how much of the screen effects may
cover — rather than anything about the update loop.

The scalars multiply authored emitter values, so content is authored
once at Epic and every lower tier is a fraction of it.

members.name: EffectsMaxActiveEmitters
members.doc: Emitters submitted per view, nearest first. 0 = unlimited.

members.name: EffectsOverdrawBudget
members.doc:
Screens of particle fill admitted per view (quad areas summed, so
overlaps count once each — that IS the overdraw). 0 = unlimited.

members.name: EnableVSM
members.doc:
Virtual Shadow Maps. Live page-management driver: each frame a
compute pass marks the virtual shadow pages under visible receivers
(from the GBuffer depth) and allocates physical pages for them. The
sparse page table is the foundation for sampling + sparse-atlas
rendering. On at Epic+ (the tier sets it). Wherever its pages cover
a reader — the deferred sun through the screen resolve, the fog
froxels and translucents through the page table — it is the
sun-shadow authority and the CSM answers only the rest; once its
cache is steady the cascades draw only what it cannot (terrain,
GPU foliage), see r.VSM.CsmCasters.

members.name: LocalVirtualShadows
members.doc:
Local-light shadows as paged virtual maps when r.Shadow.Local.Virtual
is -1; the tier sets it (FScalabilityTierValues::LocalVirtualShadows).

members.name: EnableVirtualTexture
members.doc:
Virtual texturing. A GPU-resident page table + physical atlas stream
texture pages on demand: a feedback pass records the pages the frame
sampled, the host decodes them and pulls the missing ones through a
provider a budget at a time. Drives a virtual-textured ground surface
(the integrated path). Default OFF; r.VirtualTexture forces it.

members.name: MeshletGBuffer
members.doc:
Mesh-shading GBuffer path for static meshes carrying import-built
cluster DAGs (per-meshlet frustum/cone/Hi-Z cull + screen-space-error
LOD cut). Epic+ in the tier rows; r.MeshletGBuffer overrides. Needs
VK_EXT_mesh_shader — without it every draw keeps the raster path and
GetMeshletPathState() reports why.

members.name: DepthPrepass
members.doc:
Depth prepass: eligible opaque draws lay depth down before the
G-buffer, which then loads it and shades each visible pixel once.
Pays one extra vertex pass to save the G-buffer pixel shader's
overdraw, so it is a tier choice (High+), and r.DepthPrepass
overrides. Alpha-masked, skinned, wind, WPO, crossfading and
meshlet draws are never in it (ExecuteDepthPrepass says why).

members.name: UseClusteredLighting
members.doc:
Clustered lighting (lighting upgrade). A froxel grid + GPU light culling
lets the lighting loop only the point/spot lights touching each pixel's
cluster — hundreds of lights instead of the fixed 8+8 UBO loop
(UE5/Unity-style). Default OFF — the legacy 8+8 path is the fallback.

members.name: AutoExposure
members.doc:
Auto-exposure / eye adaptation (lighting upgrade). A luminance histogram
of the HDR image drives an adapted exposure (bright scenes darken, dark
scenes brighten), like UE5/Unity. Default OFF → the manual exposure.

members.name: Atmosphere
members.doc:
Physically-based sky atmosphere (lighting upgrade). The skybox pass
raymarches single-scattering Rayleigh+Mie driven by the scene's
directional light (sun), instead of a static cubemap — horizon glow,
sunset reddening, sun disc all follow the sun direction. Default OFF.

members.name: VolumetricFog
members.doc:
Froxel volumetric fog (UE5-style). A 3D light grid is built each
frame: density from height fog + local FogVolumeComponents, in-
scattering from the sun (CSM-shadowed per froxel) + ambient through a
Henyey-Greenstein phase, temporally reprojected, integrated along Z,
then composited onto the HDR before transparency. Grid dims below come
from the scalability tier. Default OFF; `r.VolumetricFog` forces it.

members.name: VolumetricFogNear
members.doc:
Fog raymarch range in world units (froxel slices distribute
exponentially between them). Beyond FogFar the composite clamps to the
last slice, giving aerial perspective on the sky.

members.name: VolumetricClouds
members.doc:
Cloud rendering. Default OFF; `r.VolumetricClouds` forces it, and the
environment turns it on for scenes that want a sky. Which
implementation runs when it is on comes from the scalability tier:
mode 1 = the 2.5D fbm sky plane (cheap, sky pixels only), mode 2 =
the raymarched volume (Epic+, flyable, occluded by terrain). The
raymarch falls back to the plane when its resources fail to build.

members.name: CloudShadows
SSGI
members.doc:
Screen-space global illumination (GI). One-bounce indirect diffuse:
each pixel casts a few hemisphere rays, screen-space marches the depth
buffer, and gathers the lit HDR at hits as indirect light (× albedo).
Noisy by nature — TAA stabilises it. Default OFF.

members.name: EnableSDF
members.doc:
GI — world-space scene SDF. Voxelizes the static scene
into a jump-flood distance field the GI rays sphere-march. EnableSDF
builds/maintains the field; SdfDebugView replaces the screen with a
sphere-traced view of it (proves the field is correct). Default OFF.

members.name: SignedSdf
members.doc:
GI — signed-interior SDF. After the unsigned jump-flood, a parity
pass marks cells inside solid geometry and negates their distance, so
the field crosses zero at surfaces. The trilinear-interpolated signed
field reaches 0 between voxel centres (the unsigned field's interpolated
minimum can stay above eps → rays skip thin walls), killing thin-wall
GI light leaks. Needs reasonably closed geometry; default OFF.

members.name: EnableDDGI
members.doc:
GI DDGI — irradiance probes tracing the SDF for off-screen
global illumination. Implies the SDF + albedo volume. Probes update
each frame (trace + octahedral integrate); the lighting pass samples
them for indirect diffuse. Default OFF.

members.name: DdgiIntensity
members.doc:
Indirect-diffuse strength multiplier. 1.0 is physically neutral: the
radiance cache carries the Lambert 1/PI itself, so this is an artist
gain and nothing else. It used to read 0.35 (= 1/PI to within 10%)
because it was silently paying off a 1/PI the cache never applied —
which left every other consumer of that cache, reflections above all,
paying nothing and reading PI too hot.

members.name: DdgiBounce
members.doc:
Multi-bounce feedback strength: each frame the probe trace adds this
fraction of last frame's irradiance back in (cheap infinite bounce,
energy-bounded by albedo<1). 0 = single bounce. Feeds both the DDGI
probe trace and the surface radiance cache. Default 0.5.

members.name: SdfReflections
members.doc:
GI — SDF-traced reflections (off-screen glossy). Reflects the
world SDF and gathers the DDGI-lit radiance at the hit; for smooth
surfaces, composited onto the HDR. Needs the SDF + DDGI. Default OFF.

members.name: ScreenSpaceReflections
members.doc:
Tier hard off-switches: the Low preset turns the whole SSR slice
and the GTAO slice off outright (the scene's PostFX settings and
r.SSR / r.GTAO can only act within a tier that has them on).
Every consumer already handles the passes not running — the same
paths the per-scene disables exercise.

members.name: GiNearCascade
members.doc:
Optional finer near radiance cascade (Epic). A second radiance
cache baked at half the near cell (default 0.125 m) over a dim*cell
(8 m at 64^3) window centered on the camera, re-lighting the SAME
coarse SDF/albedo field. The reflection hit shading (SdfReflect +
RTReflections) samples it FIRST so near mirror/glossy reflections read
the lit surface at 2x the resolution of the 0.25 m voxel cache, and
falls back to the existing cascades outward. Epic-only; ~2 MB (64^3
RGBA16F). Preset row sets it (Epic); r.GI.NearCascade /
r.GI.NearCascade.Cell refine.

members.name: TranslucentReflections
members.doc:
One-ray reflections on forward translucent surfaces. A reflective
glass/glossy transparent casts a single mirror ray through the world
SDF clipmap, shaded from the radiance cache at the hit (sky on
miss), composited as a Fresnel-weighted specular term in the forward
shader — plus a clear-coat lobe. High/Epic (needs the SDF + radiance
cache the diffuse GI already builds); r.Reflections.Translucent gates
within. Materials opt in via a non-zero reflection intensity; water
keeps its own fresnel/refraction path untouched.

members.name: GiHwrtGather
members.doc:
Hardware ray-traced screen-probe final gather (Epic). A
ray-query variant of the screen-probe trace casts each gather ray at
the resident scene TLAS instead of sphere-marching the SDF cascade,
then shades the hit from the same radiance cache (incl. the
fine cascade) — removing SDF quantization from the near-field gather.
Gated like RT reflections: preset row sets it (Epic); r.GI.HWRTGather
gates within, and it needs the TLAS (falls back to the SDF screen-
probe trace when RT is unavailable / off / non-Epic). Implies the ray
scene (BuildRayScene). Denoised by the existing SVGF.

members.name: GiRadianceInterval
members.doc:
GI (perf) — cadence of the surface radiance cache rebuild (the
full-volume SdfRadiance dispatch, the most expensive GI pass). It only
feeds reflections, which are temporally denoised, so it can run every
Nth frame instead of every frame; a geometry change (SDF rebuild)
forces an immediate rebuild regardless. 1 = every frame. Default 4.

members.name: DdgiReactScale
members.doc:
How sharply a DDGI probe texel shortens its temporal blend when the
radiance arriving at it changes for real, so a light switching on does
not take the same ~73 frames a 1% drift does. 0 = fixed hysteresis.
r.GI.DDGI.React overrides.

members.name: ScreenSpaceSSS
members.doc:
Separable screen-space subsurface scattering (Jimenez-style). After
lighting, SSS-flagged pixels (RT3.A sss nibble) get a two-pass,
depth-aware, per-channel diffusion blur so skin reads translucent
instead of plastic. Non-SSS pixels pass through untouched. Default ON;
presets turn it on at Medium+. Default OFF so CLI test scenes (which
apply no preset) are unperturbed. Hair (Kajiya-Kay) is not gated here
— it is a per-pixel term in the lighting pass driven by the RT3 hair
flag, so it only affects hair-flagged pixels.

members.name: TierBloom
members.doc:
Tier gates on what the scene's post settings ask for: Low turns off
bloom, motion blur and contact shadows whatever the volume says.
Default on, so a renderer no preset ever touched draws what it is
told.

members.name: RTReflections
members.doc:
RT reflections (r.RTReflections). A hardware inline-ray-query
trace through the scene TLAS replaces the SSR ray march (same
temporal accumulation + Reflection_Resolve) — off-screen geometry
reflects correctly. Hit shading is the simplified hit-lighting
model (instance albedo x sun + shadow ray + irradiance ambient +
emissive, sky on miss). Falls back to SSR whenever the TLAS or ray
query is unavailable. Implies the ray scene (BuildRayScene).

members.name: RTAO
members.doc:
RT ambient occlusion (r.RTAO). Short cosine-hemisphere
occlusion rays through the TLAS replace GTAO's horizon integral at
the same composite point (raw AO target -> bilateral blur ->
lighting/reflection AO term), plus a temporal accumulation pass.
Falls back to GTAO when unavailable.

members.name: RTShadows
members.doc:
RT sun shadows (r.RTShadows). Cone-samples the sun disc through the
scene TLAS for a penumbra sized by the light's source angle, on top
of the CSM/VSM render rather than instead of it. Implies the ray
scene. Tier-driven like RTReflections/RTAO — before it was, the
per-tier RtShadowSamples numbers below tuned a pass nothing enabled.

members.name: AsyncGiUpdate
members.doc:
The GI volume update (SDF build, radiance cascades, DDGI probes) opts
into the async-compute lane, as one feature: r.GI.AsyncCompute, under
the global r.RDG.AsyncCompute. Scalability tiers do not touch it —
the frame schedule decides where it overlaps and where it joins.

members.name: ShadowMapResolution
members.doc:
Scalability NUMERIC knobs (FScalabilityTiers)
Defaults equal the historical hardcoded values, so scenes that never
apply a preset render bit-identically. ApplyQualityPreset copies the
tier row (Renderer/ScalabilityTiers.h) into these; each is then
individually overridable via its r.* cvar (applied after the preset
at BeginScene — preset sets, cvar refines).
CSM per-cascade tile resolution (atlas is a 2x2 grid of this).
Changing it live recreates the shadow atlas (WaitIdle at BeginScene).

members.name: ShadowCascadeCount
members.doc:
Directional cascades rendered/selected (1..4). The atlas stays 2x2;
unused quadrants are never rendered nor selected (splits clamp).

members.name: FoliageShadowCascades
members.doc:
CSM cascades GPU foliage casts into (0 = grass shadows off). Grass
lives inside r.Foliage.GrassDistance, so the near cascades cover it;
each extra cascade costs one cull dispatch + one indirect draw per
batch plus a per-view compacted transform pool.

members.name: MegaLights
members.doc:
MegaLights: stochastic per-pixel sampling of the shadow-casting local
lights past the atlas budget, ray/atlas/screen-space shadowed and
spatiotemporally denoised. Epic+; needs clustered lighting.

members.name: MegaLightsCheap
members.doc:
Cheap screen-space fallback shadow for atlas-denied local lights
while MegaLights is off (High/Medium tier rows): a short contact-
style depth march toward the light instead of no shadow at all.

members.name: ShadowSdfFar
members.doc:
SDF far sun shadows: cone-trace the GI global SDF past the CSM
fade band (r.Shadow.SdfFar; needs the SDF, Medium+).

members.name: RtShadowSamples
members.doc: RT sun shadow cone samples per pixel (r.RTShadows.Samples).

members.name: DdgiRaysPerProbe
members.doc:
DDGI per-frame trace budget. Changing it live recreates the DDGI
ray/irradiance buffers (history reset, WaitIdle at BeginScene).

members.name: SsgiRays
members.doc: SSGI gather budget (hemisphere rays x depth-march steps per ray).

members.name: GiDenoiseMode
members.doc:
GI/reflection temporal denoise mode: 0 = off (raw probe field
composited 1:1), 1 = SVGF-lite (velocity-aware reprojection +
disocclusion mask + variance-guided a-trous after temporal; also
upgrades the SSR temporal/spatial filter). Tier row sets it;
r.GI.Denoise refines.

members.name: GiFinalGather
members.doc:
final gather architecture: 0 = legacy per-pixel world-probe
sampling (DdgiSample), 1 = screen-space probe gather (one probe per
16 px tile + adaptive 8 px subdivision, SDF-traced, spatially
filtered between probes, bilinearly interpolated per pixel — the
world DDGI grid becomes ray source + fallback only, which removes
the probe-lattice on flat surfaces by construction). Tier row sets
it (Low/Medium = 0, High/Epic = 1); r.GI.FinalGather refines.

members.name: ScreenProbeRays
GiCardAtlasSize
members.doc:
Surface-cache card atlas edge and largest card edge; tier row sets
them, r.GI.SurfaceCache.AtlasSize / CardResolution > 0 override.

members.name: SsrMaxStepsCap
members.doc: Cap applied to the scene's ssrMaxSteps (0 = uncapped).

members.name: GtaoSlices
members.doc: GTAO horizon slices per pixel (shader default 4).

members.name: AoDivisor
members.doc:
Resolution divisor for the AO trace + horizontal AO blur. The
vertical blur stays full-res with the divided tap spacing, so it is
the joint bilateral upsample. 1 = full res.

members.name: BentNormalDivisor
members.doc:
Resolution divisor for the bent-normal filter chain (floored at
AoDivisor). Below full res the GI composite reads it through a
4-tap depth-bilateral upsample.

members.name: BloomMipCount
members.doc: Bloom mip chain length actually processed (clamped to the built 6).

members.name: DofBokeh
members.doc:
DoF blur kernel (r.DoF.Bokeh): 0 = separable gaussian, 1 = circular
disk gather with fill.

members.name: ContactShadowSteps
members.doc: Screen-space contact shadow march steps (DeferredLighting).

members.name: MaxAnisotropy
members.doc: Sampler max anisotropy clamp for newly created texture samplers.

members.name: RtReflectionRoughnessCutoff
members.doc:
RT reflections: surfaces rougher than this fall back to SDF/env
(UE-style cutoff; SSR keeps the scene's own ssrRoughnessCutoff).

members.name: RtAORays
members.doc: RT AO occlusion rays per pixel (temporal accumulation integrates).

members.name: GiProbeTraceSteps
members.doc:
sphere-march step caps per tier. Defaults equal the historical
hardcoded shader values (192/64/160 base; the far-cascade chain
extends each by its historical ratio inside the shader), so scenes
without a preset trace bit-identically. r.GI.ProbeTraceSteps /
r.GI.ScreenProbes.TraceSteps / r.GI.ReflectTraceSteps refine.

members.name: SdfResolution
members.doc:
World-SDF clipmap dimension (cubed), applied at first build. Tier row
sets it (Cinematic 128, else 64); r.GI.SDFResolution overrides.

members.name: GridSpacing
members.doc:
Minor cell size in world units. The pass LOD-steps this by powers
of ten as the camera climbs (SceneRenderer::ResolveGridSpacing), so
this is the size at ground level, not a fixed screen density.

members.name: GridMajorEvery
members.doc:
Minor cells per major line. 10 is the decimal convention every DCC
package uses, which is what makes a hand-typed coordinate readable
off the viewport.

members.name: GridPlaneHeight
members.doc: World Y the plane sits at.

members.name: GridFadeStart
members.doc:
Distance at which the grid begins fading and where it is gone. 0 =
derive both from the resolved cell size, which keeps a grid drawn
at 1 cm and one drawn at 100 m equally legible.

members.name: GridAxisWidth
members.doc:
Axis line half-width in pixels — the X/Z axes are the only lines
that say where the origin is, so they are drawn wider than a cell
line rather than merely tinted.

members.name: GridAxisXColor
members.doc:
The transform gizmo's X and Z colours (FTransformGizmoDraw), so the
axis line under an arrow is the arrow's own colour. Y is up here, so
the ground plane's axes are X and Z — UE's red/green floor axes are
its Z-up X and Y.

types.name: SceneRenderer::EMeshletPathState
types.doc:
Why the meshlet GBuffer path is or is not running. The fallback to the
classic raster path is never silent: the first frame that wants
meshlets and cannot have them logs the reason once, and this reports it
for the rest of the session (editor stats, tests, bug reports).

members.name: Disabled
members.doc: tier row + r.MeshletGBuffer both say no

members.name: NoMeshShaderSupport
members.doc: device lacks VK_EXT_mesh_shader

members.name: NoPipeline
members.doc: extension present, pipeline/shader failed to build

types.name: SceneRenderer::FGiCardCoverage
types.doc:
What the last coverage census found. Samples is 0 until a census has both
dispatched and been read back, so a caller can tell "nothing measured yet"
from "measured, nothing covered" — the two used to be one number, and a
census that never ran reads as total failure.

A miss splits three ways because the repairs differ: no record filed near
the surface is a BUDGET miss, a record near it whose box misses it is a
card-SET miss, and a box that claims it whose texel the lookup rejects is
a CAPTURE miss.

members.name: Samples
members.doc: opaque GBuffer samples taken

members.name: Covered
members.doc: a card answered the consumers' own lookup

members.name: InCell
members.doc: the sample's index cell held at least one record

members.name: Claimed
members.doc: some resident record's box contained the sample on the face its normal names

members.name: NoTexel
members.doc: of those, the furthest any candidate got was a tile texel the capture never wrote

members.name: BadNormal
members.doc: ... a texel whose captured normal faces away from the surface

members.name: BadDepth
members.doc: ... a texel whose captured depth puts the surface somewhere else

members.name: BadNormalDegenerate
members.doc: of BadNormal, the ones whose stored normal is zero rather than merely wrong

members.name: BadDepthTexelWouldAnswer
members.doc: BadNormal by the box face the lookup chose

members.name: BadDepthNearMiss
members.doc: of BadDepth, the ones inside twice the tolerance — a tolerance or projection that drifted, as against a card holding a different surface entirely

types.name: SceneRenderer::FSdfCpuSnapshot
types.doc:
The same field as one consistent value for a DIFFERENT thread. The
game thread produces the next frame while the render thread consumes
this one, and the render thread can resize the SDF (a Cinematic tier
change takes it from 64 to 128) between a reader's size query and its
copy — reading the live members from the game thread walked off a
64-cubed buffer with a 128-cubed index. The render thread publishes a
snapshot at the end of its SDF pass, only while someone has asked for
one; the reader copies it under the lock and gets the last frame's
field, dimension, cell size and origin together.

types.name: SceneRenderer::FSdfFieldInfo
types.doc:
The GPU-samplable half, published every frame (it is a handful of
words and a reference): the volume the GPU particle collision binds
must not be copied from the live member while the render thread may
be releasing it.

types.name: SceneRenderer::FLazyWarmGates
types.doc:
Which of the startup warm's four memory-heavy groups this configuration
actually wants. Read from the cvars alone, because the warm runs before
any scene is open and there are no render options to resolve a "code
default" against.

types.name: SceneRenderer::FHeavyFeatureResidency
types.doc:
What this renderer holds for the features the project switches gate
(FProjectRenderFeatures): a project that leaves one off must show false
here after any number of frames at any tier, not merely skip a dispatch.

types.name: SceneRenderer::FViewTargetMemory
types.doc:
The persistent render-resolution targets the bound view holds outside
the frame graph: how many images and their bytes (mip 0, one sample).

types.name: SceneRenderer::FPostChainRuns
types.doc:
How often each pass r.RDG.PostChain moves has recorded, on either path,
since the renderer was created — a bench that A/Bs the switch checks the
passes it times actually ran.

types.name: FSurfaceCode
types.doc:
CPU mirror of the G-Buffer's RT3.A surface code — the lane that decides
which BRDF a pixel is shaded with. It is a TWO-TIER code, not a flat
3-bit-model + 5-bit-scalar split:

tier 0..6  the classic shading models, low 5 bits = that model's custom
scalar. Byte for byte what FLightChannels::PackRT3A has always
produced — the material row asserts the two agree over every
reachable (model, custom) pair, which is the proof no shipped
material's G-Buffer byte moved.
tier 7     the escape. The low 5 bits name an extended model slot instead
of a scalar (slot 1..31 = ids 8..38) and the surface's per-pixel
payload moves to RT3.R/G — 16 bits, where the classic tier only
had 5 and spent R/G on clear coat.

Slot 0 is reserved: it produces byte 0xE0, which is precisely the byte the
old encoder produced for model 7, and which the lighting pass already fell
through to plain DefaultLit for. That is why the escape cannot disturb a
shipped pixel, and why an id past the last slot degrades to it instead of
aliasing onto a real model.

The point of the tier is that the id ceiling stops being the blocker: a
ninth shading model is now an enum value plus a decode branch, not a
G-Buffer re-encoding. It is also the code point a per-pixel indirection
would claim — an extended slot whose RT3.R/G is a 16-bit record index into
a surface-parameter buffer rather than two payload bytes.

Mirrors GBufferFill.hlsl (encode) and DeferredLighting.hlsl (decode).

members.name: UnpackCustom
members.doc:
An escaped pixel has no scalar lane left — its payload is RT3.R/G, so
reading the low bits as a 0..1 value there would return the slot index.

members.name: NoRecord
members.doc:
The escape's 16 bits, used as a RECORD INDEX rather than as a payload.
RT3.R is the low byte and RT3.G the high one, so the two lanes the
classic tier spends on clear coat become one 0..65535 index into the
frame's surface-parameter buffer. kNoRecord is what the uber (non-graph)
path writes: it has no entry reserved, and indexing record 0 there would
shade the pixel from an unrelated material's parameters.

members.signature: static void PackRecordIndex(uint32_t index, uint8_t& outR, uint8_t& outG)

members.name: UnpackRecordIndex
members.signature: static uint32_t UnpackRecordIndex(uint8_t r, uint8_t g)

members.name: InstanceRecordIndex
members.signature: static uint32_t InstanceRecordIndex(uint32_t base, uint32_t instanceOrdinal)
members.doc:
An instanced draw's record index: the group's base plus the instance's
own ordinal within the draw. The CPU mirror of what GBufferFill.hlsl's
INSTANCED permutation computes in the vertex stage, and it exists so
the two cannot drift — nothing about an off-by-one here fails to
compile, it just hands one eyeball the eyeball next to it.

Clamping to the sentinel is what makes the sentinel survive the add: a
group with no block pushes NoRecord as its base, and NoRecord + ordinal
must still read as "no record" rather than as an index past the pool.

types.name: FSurfaceRecord
types.doc:
CPU mirror of one surface-parameter record — what an extended surface gets
INSTEAD of a packed lane. Five float4s, indexed by the 16 bits RT3.R/G carry
for an escaped pixel, produced fresh each frame by
SceneRenderer::BuildGBufferDrawPlan and uploaded by
SceneRenderer::UpdateSurfaceParamsForFrame; read by DeferredLighting.hlsl.

Model is stored in the record and re-checked against the surface code at
decode time. The index and the record are written by two different passes a
frame apart in the pipeline; if a shading model ever escapes with a stale or
unreserved index, shading it from whatever record happens to sit there is
silent corruption, whereas a model mismatch is a fallback the pass can take.

Lanes 2..4 are the PER-DRAW half and the reason the key moved off the
material: the eyeball's world pivot and its world gaze axis come from the
draw's own model matrix, so two eyeballs sharing a material no longer share
a stare. They are also what makes an iris/sclera split possible at all in a
deferred pass, which has a world position per pixel but no UV.

members.name: PoolCap
members.doc:
How many records one frame can mint. It must stay BELOW the no-record
sentinel: a full pool that handed out 0xFFFF would name the one index
that means "shade from the defaults", so the overflow path and the
fallback path would become indistinguishable.

4096 was the per-DRAW bound, and a scene reaches it only by submitting
four thousand extended draws. Records are now per INSTANCE, and
auto-instancing exists precisely because a scene holds hundreds of
copies of one mesh: a single instanced group of eyeballs can spend as
many records as the whole frame used to. The cap is the fan-out
headroom, not the allocation — the buffer grows to the records actually
minted (UpdateSurfaceParamsForFrame), so a scene with no extended
surface still pays a few kilobytes.

members.doc:
Written into IrisCosOuter when the material authored no iris cone. A
cosine can never legally reach it, so the lighting pass reads it as
"the whole surface is iris" — the behaviour every eye had before the
mask existed, which is what keeps the mask's default free.

The five float4 lanes exactly as DeferredLighting.hlsl reads them. The
producer and the codec test both go through here, so a lane cannot be

fails to compile, it just shades wrong.

The one place a draw's transform is folded into its record. Both the
plan and the codec test go through it, because the two things that make
the record per-draw — the world pivot and the world gaze axis — are

The gaze axis is transformed by the model's 3x3 rather than its inverse
transpose on purpose: it is a direction along the mesh, not a normal to
it, so a non-uniformly scaled eyeball must carry it the way the geometry
goes.

types.name: FSkyAmbient
types.doc:
The single authority for "what colour is the sky, and how much light does
it put into the scene". The shader draws the gradient / the atmosphere's
sky-view LUT per pixel; the renderer integrates the same functions here on
the CPU to get the flat radiance the GI probe-miss and the no-IBL ambient
fall back to. One source is what keeps the visible sky and the lighting sky
from drifting apart.

Keep FallbackSkyRadiance in lockstep with SkyGradient in Sky/SkyDraw.hlsli,
and the atmosphere with Sky/Atmosphere.hlsli through FSkyAtmosphereModel.
The sky-ambient and sky-agreement self-tests lock the numbers.

Gradient fallback sky, driven by the scene's sky colour (= ambientColor *
ambientIntensity, interpreted as the sky's average radiance). Returns the
radiance looking along dir.

Solid-angle average of FallbackSkyRadiance. By construction this returns
skyColor — the gradient shape is normalized so that the sky you see and
the sky that lights you are one number.

in engine radiance units: the sky-view LUT's value times the sun's colour,
intensity, ATMO_SKY_RADIANCE_SCALE and the sky luminance factor.

types.name: FSkyAtmosphereModel
types.doc:
The atmosphere as a physical model (Hillaire, "A Scalable and Production
Ready Sky and Atmosphere Rendering Technique", 2020): Rayleigh and Mie
scattering, ozone absorption, a transmittance LUT and a multiple-scattering
LUT. The GPU passes (Sky/Atmosphere.hlsli and the Sky/*Lut compute shaders)
integrate the same functions over the same parameterisations; this CPU copy
is what the GI ambient, the sun's transmittance tint and the agreement tests
read, so the sky the scene is lit by is the sky it shows.

Radiance here is luminance per unit sun illuminance. The renderer multiplies
by the sun's colour, its intensity and ATMO_SKY_RADIANCE_SCALE.

types.name: FSynthBenchmark
types.doc:
A measured answer to "how fast is this machine", the SynthBenchmark
analogue: two fixed GPU workloads (an ALU-bound fma chain and a
bandwidth-bound stream over a 64 MB buffer) and one single-thread CPU
workload, each sized to run for a fixed slice of time and scored against a
reference part, so 100 on either index is a mid-range 2020 desktop and a
number is comparable across runs, drivers and backends. The auto-tier
reads the indices before it consults the GPU name list, which can only
know the cards that existed when it was written.

A result is cached in the per-user engine config keyed by the GPU name and
the core count, so the player benchmarks on its first launch and never
again until the hardware changes; the editor runs it only from the
Quality menu's Benchmark button.

195 Mops/s (index ~115). The CPU workload is a dependent hash and
gather chain, so it follows clock and cache latency, not vector width.

types.name: FVdbVolume
types.doc:
A sparse volume from a NanoVDB file (.nvdb — what Houdini, Blender and
EmberGen export smoke, fire and clouds as), resampled into a dense brick the
renderer ray-marches: density, and temperature when the file carries it.

The grids are sampled on the CPU at load time, trilinearly and box-filtered
down to MaxResolution along the longest axis, so the GPU side is one RG16F
Texture3D sampled with hardware filtering on every backend — no PNanoVDB
tree walk in a shader, which would have needed raw buffer access that
D3D11 and the Metal cross-compile do not share. The price is resolution:
a volume wider than MaxResolution voxels loses detail, and the empty space
of a sparse grid costs memory inside its bounding box.

Only uncompressed files load (the vendored NanoVDB has no ZIP / Blosc); a
compressed one is refused with its codec named. Float and quantised
(Fp4 / Fp8 / Fp16 / FpN) grids are read. The grid's index-to-world map is
taken as scale + translation — a rotated grid transform is not applied.

types.name: FVolumetricClouds
types.doc:
Raymarched volumetric-cloud math shared between the CPU (resource sizing,
the headless self-test) and the GPU (Volumetrics/CloudCommon.hlsli mirrors
these exactly). The cloud layer is a world-space altitude slab; the march
walks the segment of the view ray inside it, so the same helpers decide the
slab entry/exit, the vertical density profile, the step budget and the
energy-conserving multi-scatter octaves. Every method is pure.

members.name: SlabIntersect
members.signature: static bool SlabIntersect(const Vec3& origin, const Vec3& dir, float baseAltitude, float topAltitude, float& outEnter, float& outExit)
members.doc:
Intersects a ray with the horizontal slab [baseAltitude, topAltitude].
Returns false when the ray never enters the slab (parallel outside it,
or pointing away). outEnter/outExit are distances along dir, clamped to
>= 0 so a camera inside the slab starts at 0.

members.name: HeightFraction
members.signature: static float HeightFraction(float worldY, float baseAltitude, float topAltitude)
members.doc: Normalized altitude inside the slab, 0 at the base and 1 at the top.

members.name: HeightGradient
members.signature: static float HeightGradient(float heightFraction, float cloudType)
members.doc:
Vertical density profile. cloudType blends stratus (0, flat low sheet)
through stratocumulus (0.5) to cumulus (1, tall billowing towers): the
gradient widens and shifts up with the type. Zero at both slab edges so
clouds never clip against the layer boundary.

members.signature: static float ShapeToDensity(float shapeNoise, float coverage, float heightFraction, float cloudType, float density)
members.doc:
Coverage remap: the raw [0,1] shape noise is thresholded by coverage and
renormalized, so coverage 0 clears the sky and 1 overcasts it. The result
is scaled by the height gradient and the layer density.

members.signature: static uint32_t StepCount(float segmentLength, float maxDistance, uint32_t minSteps, uint32_t maxSteps)
members.doc:
Adaptive step count for a march segment. Short segments (grazing the slab

gets the maximum. Always in [minSteps, maxSteps].

members.signature: static void MultiScatterOctave(uint32_t octave, float attenuation, float contribution, float eccentricity, float& outExtinction, float& outScatter, float& outEccentricity)
members.doc:

each successive octave scales extinction by attenuation^n, the scattering
